- Передаваемый продуктовый baseline — .216 / versionCode 335, source commit b43bfb64; APK [DocScan-0.4.216.apk](../dist/DocScan-0.4.216.apk), SHA-256 4b187e4254a91edddd29efc155f3d1d79c9548bc8a809eb71c7c0ea263aa030c. - На .216 имеется полный API 36.1 connected suite 139/139, подписанная сборка и .215→.216 update-preservation evidence: [чеклист](../execution/device_tests/0.4.216/CHECKLIST.md), [PDF import boundary report](../execution/evidence/ENG-PDF-PUBLISH-DIRSYNC-ENOSPC-0.4.216.md). Это подтверждает названные проверки на эмуляторе; физическую квалификацию и приёмку не подтверждает.
- Исправленный exact-source check_all на harness commit 7434fd03 завершился с кодом 0 как non-strict проверка. Он явно показывает B1–B9 IN_PROGRESS, Q и A BLOCKED, восемь harness tasks IN_PROGRESS, а также 48 BR без AC-связей, 213 требований без positive mapping и product crash matrix 0/230: [отчёт](../execution/evidence/ENG-GATE-STATUS-01.md). Код 0 здесь не означает прохождение gate.

Модель запущена как rus+eng; испанская строка потеряла ñ, ó, ü, ú, а нормализующий oracle их не проверяет. Отчёт: [ENG-OCR-02](../execution/evidence/ENG-OCR-02-current-cyrillic-spanish-0.4.216.md). Испанская поддержка и автоматическое определение языка пока не являются доказанным результатом.
- Аудит .212–.216 не обесценивает уже полученные результаты пяти названных PDF fault boundaries. Он меняет следующий способ работы: оставшиеся границы этого класса сначала собрать в один полный индекс применимости и пакетный контракт; не выпускать отдельную APK и не повторять весь дорогой цикл только ради очередного соседнего fault seam.

### Предлагаемый порядок и правило пакетирования

1. После утверждения карты — один evidence-led readiness пакет B1–B9/Q/A и единый запрос по перечисленным owner/reviewer/device inputs. Для зависимых задач не делать следующую правку продукта до Gate A; независимая работа по traceability inventory и внешним подготовкам может идти параллельно.
2. После Gate A — P0 → P1 → P2 → P3 → P4 → P5 → P6. T9.1/T9.2 собираются по ходу по тем же контрактам; T9.3/T9.4 закрываются на финальном candidate. Затем P7.
3. До каждого code batch фиксировать один класс/пользовательский результат, полный применимый inventory, положительный и отрицательный oracle, affected set и заранее заданное условие закрытия. PDF .212–.216 и иные уже валидные evidence positions индексируются и переиспользуются.
4. Во время работы разрешены адресные affected-set проверки. Полный connected suite, exact-source check_all, signed APK/hash/signature и update-preservation прогон выполняются один раз на завершённом согласованном installable candidate, а не после каждого соседнего fault injection. Продуктовый version bump и отдельный commit сохраняются для каждого законченного code batch согласно Git rules; harness-only/evidence-only work не получает фиктивную продуктовую версию.
5. Если acceptance input отсутствует, строка остаётся BLOCKED/NOT RUN с причиной и следующим конкретным входом. Не менять статусы и пороги из-за отсутствия доступа; не называть весь MVP готовым на основании subset.

### Решения, требующие отдельного подтверждения владельца

- **DEC-Q:** подтвердить ли описанные в листе решений последствия ручной установки APK + приложения «Самопроверка» на Xiaomi без qualification по исходному количественному протоколу. Если да, явно сохранить ограничения заявления о проверке; если нет — требуется физический qualification path по протоколу.
- **DEC-REVIEW:** подтвердить независимый review и назначить доступную сторону/процесс. Review не может быть самоотчётом исполнителя.
- **INPUT-03 / DEC-OCR-LANG:** утвердить language/script envelope, отдельно Spanish yes/no. Имеющееся испанское smoke evidence не даёт ответа о продуктовой поддержке.
- **INPUT-02 и CONFLICT-01/03/04/05/06:** пройти только решения, влияющие на открытые зависимые строки P1–P6; уже записанные делегированные инженерные решения не переоткрывать без причины. Нерешённые retention, dirty-state, UnknownOutcome, tombstone и quality decisions оставить в реестре с authority, потерями и затронутыми этапами.
- **INPUT-06/07 и provider tuple:** предоставить Product Contract/Architecture authority, физический Xiaomi + OS, и квалифицируемый primary: SAF destination tuple. INPUT-04 implementation default и INPUT-05 destination scope не считать доказательством физического качества или tuple acceptance.

**Запрашиваемое утверждение:** принять этот конечный список и порядок пакетов как рабочую карту закрытия, не меняющую критерии и текущие статусы. До утверждения карта является предложением; MVP остаётся IN_PROGRESS_NOT_ACCEPTED, а дальнейшие кодовые изменения по новому пакету не начинаются.

### Историческая формулировка DR-03-вопроса (заменена решением 5.355)

Исторические варианты ниже отражают revisions 5.353–5.354 и не являются активным запросом: revision 5.355 разрешил выбор в пределах делегированных системно-инженерных полномочий.

Источник: UFS `BR-002-09`/`AC-002-06`, `BR-009-13`, `BR-010-08`; рекомендация листа владельца DR-03; ограничение SAF из `docs/platform-constraints-audit.txt` §12. **Рекомендация:** строгое fail-closed поведение, если для тяжёлого импорта или Save невозможно получить пригодную оценку/ёмкость: не начинать соответствующую операцию и не менять workspace. Оно ближе к рекомендации DR-03 об отказе до изменений, но может блокировать корректные файлы и SAF providers без size/quota metadata.

Подтвердите один вариант:

1. Принять рекомендацию DR-03 (сумма известных ожидаемых размеров + 100 MB); если оценку/ёмкость нельзя надёжно получить — не начинать операцию, оставить workspace без изменений.
2. Применять порог только там, где размеры и свободное место измеримы; при неизвестных SAF/provider значениях продолжать с явной неопределённостью и полагаться на существующую обработку реальной ошибки записи. Это допускает поздний recoverable failure и не даёт универсальной гарантии preflight.
3. Задать другой точный fallback для неизвестных значений.

Затронутые решения/работы: import `BR-002-09`/`AC-002-06`, T5.2/CAP-002; Save `BR-009-13`/`BR-010-08`, T6/CAP-009/010. Остальные независимые строки карты и Gate readiness продолжаются; ответ не меняет автоматически ни acceptance thresholds, ни текущие статусы.

Execution result (revision 5.354, 2026-09-27) — ENG-IMPORT-SPACE-PREFLIGHT-01 source-audit preparation:
- Source finding, finite test inventory, owner decision options and matching ledger/handoff/traceability updates committed as `88197e42` (documentation only; product code and version unchanged).
- `git diff --check` passed; `python3 execution/tools/validate_traceability.py` passed with exact source/CSV IDs and evidence paths: 16 CAP, 146 BR, 84 AC; 48 BR lack AC linkage; 17 scoped positive mappings, 17 negative/guard references, 213 requirements without positive mapping; product crash checks remain 0/230. CSV SHA-256: `4ed0285bff3b14294052389fa76f05384b85760d53035ca6eaccac98d4a85341`. Product ledger JSON parsing passed; T5.2 remains PARTIAL and MVP remains IN_PROGRESS_NOT_ACCEPTED.
- This closes only the source-audit and contract-preparation step. Low-space runtime tests, product implementation, DR-03, Gate A, physical qualification, independent review and parent T5.2/CAP-002 acceptance are NOT RUN/open. Continue independent Gate-readiness/traceability work; ask owner to resolve the DR-03 fallback before preflight implementation.

Execution decision (revision 5.355, 2026-09-28) — ENG-DR-03-01:
- The user's direct instruction dated 2026-09-28 delegates system-engineering choices for this project and says not to stop for user approval. This resolves the pending DR-03 implementation choice only; it does not change scope, frozen invariants, acceptance criteria, gate authority, or owner-sheet checkbox history. This revision supersedes the DR-03 question/options in 5.353 and the “ask owner” next step in 5.354.
- **Selected policy:** for each heavy operation before writing to DocScan-managed storage, measure available bytes on the exact managed filesystem. When all applicable sizes are known and valid, require their sum + decimal 100,000,000-byte reserve. When one or more sizes are unknown/unreliable, use the sum of known sizes + that reserve as a lower bound, mark the estimate incomplete, do not report “space is sufficient”, and proceed if the lower bound fits. If the managed-volume query fails, or the known lower bound + reserve exceeds available bytes, fail before publication intent, staging, ImportSession/Page or workspace mutation. An unobservable SAF destination quota is UNKNOWN; it does not block solely for lack of provider metadata. Preflight the app-private composition volume and retain existing provider verification, source-consumption barriers and UNKNOWN_OUTCOME recovery. Real provider ENOSPC after start remains possible and must fail safely.
- **Basis and trade-off:** Android's shared-storage guide states `OpenableColumns.SIZE` may be null for remote content; `StatFs.getAvailableBytes()` measures bytes available on a specified filesystem path. Sources: [Android shared-storage guide](https://developer.android.com/training/data-storage/shared/documents-files), [Android `StatFs` API](https://developer.android.com/reference/android/os/StatFs.html). Best-effort handling avoids rejecting valid SAF sources only because metadata is omitted; it loses a universal guarantee against late ENOSPC when source size/provider quota is unknown. The existing `.212`–`.216` injection results remain separate cleanup evidence and do not prove this policy.
- **Change record:** `unknown size/quota → proceed after measured managed-volume reserve, with estimate-incomplete disclosure`; reason: platform APIs do not guarantee complete metadata for SAF remote sources. Execution contract amendment (revision 5.360, 2026-09-28) — `ENG-RUNNER-INSTRUMENTATION-EXIT-01`:
- **Reason for amendment:** revision 5.359 incorrectly classified `INSTRUMENTATION_CODE: -1` as a failure. Official Android API documentation defines `RESULT_OK = -1`; Android tooling tests also show that a final `INSTRUMENTATION_CODE: -1` can represent successful instrumentation even with no tests. This corrects the signal interpretation while preserving the false-acceptance finding and full test scope.
- **Requirement/user result:** Gate B1/B2; `AUDIT_INVARIANTS.md` I11/I21/I22; FROZEN Spike Protocol v1.1 §3.5. Snapshot and aggregate must each have completed the targeted single S1 test successfully and the adb process must exit zero before their result is accepted.
- **Baseline:** source remains unchanged at harness commit `6594f487`, `host/runner.py` v1.6, SHA-256 `e527d6248190235b2b515f9609d8ef254be57a6ff717c0a2308789d9ea265bf4`; product `.216` / code 335. The 5.359 rejection-of-`-1` condition is superseded by this amendment; no source implementation or regression has run yet.
- **Contract:** for both S1 snapshot and aggregate, require adb `returncode == 0`, exact positive summary `OK (1 test)`, and absence of `FAILURES!!!`, `INSTRUMENTATION_FAILED`, or `INSTRUMENTATION_ABORTED`. If `INSTRUMENTATION_CODE` is present, it must be `-1`; `-1` is valid only alongside the expected test summary and never substitutes for it. `OK (0 tests)`, a nonzero adb return with positive-looking output, or any other explicit instrumentation code fails closed. Android references: [Activity.RESULT_OK](https://developer.android.com/reference/android/app/Activity#RESULT_OK) and [Android instrumentation result parser tests](https://android.googlesource.com/platform/tools/base/+/088f74c4fa52d08871b31635be96ab8ae05c87bb%5E!/).
- **Required controls:** per boundary, zero-exit `OK (1 test)` with no final code and with `INSTRUMENTATION_CODE: -1` passes; nonzero-exit plus `OK (1 test)`, code `-1` without test summary, `OK (0 tests)`, explicit code other than `-1`, failure/abort marker all fail before later success-dependent steps. Preserve the intentionally killed `start_case` process path (code 0 is expected there only with matching marker, PID and `/proc` death evidence), plus S2–S6 controls.
- **Action and acceptance:** update only host runner S1 snapshot/aggregate checks and orchestrator regressions; bump runner 1.6→1.7. Acceptance requires all mapped controls, existing intentional-kill and protected-analogue controls, focused tests, then one complete configured host/build/migration/traceability/ledger/non-strict-gate pass on the final source with checksummed raw evidence. Product version, frozen thresholds, gate/task/CAP statuses and acceptance authority remain unchanged. Independent review and one new DEV cycle remain required for B1/B2; full I01–I25 inventory is still open.

Engineering decision / inventory update (revision 5.387, 2026-09-28) — frozen aggregate outcome vocabulary:
- **Source and authority:** `docs/02_DocScan_Spike_Protocol_v1.1_FROZEN_Xiaomi14Ultra.md` §2.5 defines `FAIL` only for an observed kill-condition and `INCOMPLETE` for missing mandatory work/result/evidence; S2 §4.6 lists six kill counters; S4 §6.6 explicitly says an app-validator failure that prevents commit is not itself a correctness breach. This is `AUTH-A` as a logical consequence of the frozen specification and is recorded as `ENG-AGGREGATE-OUTCOME-01` in `execution/decisions.md`; it adds no threshold, scope, or user decision.
- **Decision:** a typed operation failure alone does not force aggregate `FAIL`. Keep its per-run record and count; a completed full workload may be `PASS` if all required evidence exists and no frozen kill occurred. Missing/unobservable mandatory work is `INCOMPLETE`; a listed kill is `FAIL`. Apply this across S1–S6, including S1-only implementation extensions and the generic aggregate-PASS/per-run loop. Preserve the typed failure as visible in final package metrics. Owner acceptance/gates remain unchanged.
- **Current source impact:** `S1` disk aggregation promotes any non-PASS run/false artifact check to FAIL; `S2Harness` promotes typed failures, accepted/committed mismatch, failed health observation, background error, and unconfirmed permit overlap to kill status; `S4Harness` promotes any app-validator failure/failed run to aggregate FAIL; common `validate_dir` rejects aggregate PASS on any per-run FAIL or false artifact check. Align by retaining complete typed failures as counted results, mapping only explicit frozen kill conditions to FAIL, and treating missing/unobservable mandatory work as INCOMPLETE. These are source deviations for the unified I12/I13 package, not grounds to relax or add thresholds.
- **Required proof:** complete PASS, typed-failure PASS, missing-work INCOMPLETE, and exact listed-kill FAIL fixtures for S2/S4; analogous outcome/counter controls for all other spikes; each case must assert exact per-run/aggregate values, no later false status, and evidence preservation. No new tests were run in this decision pass; see `AUDIT_INVARIANTS.md` §§11.15–11.16.
- **Next:** finish remaining finite I01–I25 property/mode/evidence cells, then include this decision in the single full runner/harness batch and its single complete verification cycle. B1/B2 remain `IN_PROGRESS_NOT_ACCEPTED` / `REVIEW_REQUIRED`; physical Q, independent review, and owner acceptance remain outstanding.

Execution contract clarification (revision 5.435, 2026-09-29) — S2 latency source limits:
- `request_to_tx_commit_ms` is an integer in the per-run source record, produced as `(tTxCommitNs - tIntakeNs)/1_000_000`; S2Harness does not serialize `tTxCommitNs` or an independent commit timestamp in the row/raw log. - Empty successful-observation population is source-backed only when every row in that workload is an explicit typed capture failure with both latency metrics exactly `-1`; the producer's percentile helper returns `0` on an empty list. This preserves Protocol §§2.5/4.4: typed failure alone is not a frozen kill. Any missing row or invalid metric remains invalid/incomplete per the existing required-work matrix; no threshold is introduced. Run outcomes and aggregate FAIL remain derived under existing frozen kill semantics.
- Tests must cover the 18 aggregate fields independently, all source domains and page-visible endpoint drift, a percentile fixture that distinguishes nearest rank from floor indexing, exact typed-failure sentinel exclusion (including all-failure population), and a complete QUAL source set while retaining the exact 20×100 matrix. ### Inventory amendment (revision 5.457, 2026-09-29) — nested async OCR permit ownership

- **Observed after display fix:** all 30 S2 operations now commit and pass C7 with zero typed failures, but the suite remains `INCOMPLETE` at its PASS assertion. C-W0 and C-W2 boundaries validate; C-W1 has no background error or capture waits.
- **Source diagnosis:** Frozen Protocol v1.1 §4.4 requires one real OCR job to hold the sole permit for the capture interval. `S2Harness` creates that outer C-W1 permit, then calls `OcrAdapter.recognizeText` as a nested job. ML Kit completes asynchronously on a different callback thread; `HeavyWorkScheduler.release` treats this nested callback as an unrelated top-level release whenever the owner thread differs, releases the semaphore, and loses the intended outer permit interval. Runtime timings plus source call/ownership paths agree. This is an I15 scheduler ownership defect, not an emulator camera limitation.
- **Correction/inventory:** in `HeavyWorkScheduler.release`, an asynchronous non-owner release matching a nested lease closes only that nested reservation while preserving the owner permit and active-job count; only the owner’s final release drops the semaphore and emits final permit release. Add instrumentation positives for asynchronous nested release and ordinary top-level async release, plus budget-denial/no-leak controls. Preserve byte accounting and no-wait capture semantics. Search all nested acquire/release analogues; verify OCR and PDF scheduler use.
- **Affected set/version:** `app/src/main/java/com/example/docscanspike/HeavyWorkScheduler.java`, `app/src/main/java/com/example/docscanspike/S2Harness.java` only as needed, `app/src/androidTest/java/com/example/docscanspike/D1EncoderFinishedInstrumentedTest.java`, app harness `.1.23`/code24→`.1.24`/code25. No product `.219`/338, host runner or acceptance threshold changes.

# Методология системного аудита валидатора

Версия документа: 1.1. Основание: инструкция пользователя от 2026-09-20.
Это проектное приложение к [общему регламенту взаимодействия](docs/AGENT_COLLABORATION_PROTOCOL.md),
а не универсальная инструкция для других задач. Формы передачи:
[AGENT_COLLABORATION_TEMPLATES.md](docs/AGENT_COLLABORATION_TEMPLATES.md).
Исходный код для начальной инвентаризации: `e5eede6`.
Статус: **IN_PROGRESS — полнота инвентаризации и покрытия ещё не подтверждена**.

## 1.1 Активный срез аудита — resume evidence integrity (2026-09-28)

Этот ограниченный срез относится к Gate B1/B2 и предшествует исправлению
`cmd_resume`. Проверяемая база: harness commit `10108e9cf58f868bb147f99ba8b9e5f6baa9a4b7`,
`host/runner.py` v1.5 (SHA-256
`6388b82f062dfc9fab405d2820b6d86600449b4452f8610bb61bc70a74c51085`), product
`.216` / versionCode 335. Нормативы: этот документ §§1–7 (I07, I21–I23),
`docs/AGENT_COLLABORATION_PROTOCOL.md` §§3–5 и существующая схема
`resume_attempts.json` в `validate_dir`.

**Сценарий пользователя:** инженер возобновляет прерванный DEV/qualification цикл.
До любой команды устройству runner обязан сохранить исходные evidence/attempts,
проверить их целостность и подтвердить, что запускает тот же цикл на том же
устройстве и APK. Ошибку чтения нельзя превращать в пустую историю или считать
отсутствием evidence.

**Найденные места для проверки одним классом (P/F/C/E):**

| Место в baseline `host/runner.py` | Роль и статус проверки |
|---|---|
| `cmd_resume` ~2638–2639 | Исключение при чтении любого cycle JSON игнорируется; проверяется, может ли runner начать ADB/device работу до последующего `validate_dir`. |
| `cmd_resume` ~2696–2704 | Существующий `resume_attempts.json` при parse/read exception заменяется `[]`; это может стереть журнал при следующей записи. Дефект подтверждён чтением кода; runtime regression ещё не запускался. |
| `build_s1_aggregate_from_disk` ~2353–2371 | Metadata candidate files перебираются с fallback. Это допустимо только для необязательного/восстановимого источника; malformed JSON остаётся видимым `validate_dir`, а старый aggregate пересобирается из per-run evidence. Проверить побочные действия и сохранить как исключение либо включить в исправление на основе теста. |
| `cmd_package` ~2880–2894 | Копирование raw log пропускает исключение, но последующий `validate_dir` проверяет каждую JSON ссылку и fail-closed при отсутствующем mandatory log; исходный цикл остаётся нетронут. Защищённый аналог при подтверждении регрессией валидатора. |
| `validate_dir` ~797–799, `cmd_verify_gates` ~2249–2255, evidence-log readers ~335–337 и ~764–766, dump reader ~1135–1140 | Parse/read failure заканчивается ошибкой, без fallback к PASS. Защищённые аналоги. |
| `cmd_resume` ~2717–2727 | Повреждённые per-run файлы сохраняются и записываются как failed attempt; не удалять и не заменять это поведение. Защищённый аналог. |
| `_execute_single_s1_case` ~402–414 | Ошибка разбора PID игнорируется только до обязательной проверки `pid is None`, которая вызывает fail-closed; не принимать текстовый маркер за успешно проверенную смерть. Защищённый аналог. |

**Положительные/отрицательные сценарии до кода:**

1. Нет журнала попыток: resume создаёт новый список попыток; существующий end-to-end сценарий остаётся валидным.
2. Корректный непустой журнал: прежние записи логически сохраняются, новая попытка добавляется, outcome меняется только после `validate_dir`.
3. Malformed/truncated attempts JSON, top-level не-list, entry не-object, отсутствующий обязательный ключ, недопустимый mode/outcome или I/O read failure: resume завершает работу до ADB/device-команды; исходные байты остаются неизменными.
4. Повреждённый cycle JSON при наличии другого пригодного identity JSON: resume завершает работу до ADB/device-команды; повреждённый файл остаётся байт-в-байт неизменным, прежние записи журнала сохраняются и добавляется одна запись `FAILED`.
5. Корректные identity + невалидный отдельный per-run JSON: не запускать недостающие cases до обнаружения corruption; сохранить исходный файл и прежние записи журнала, добавив одну запись `FAILED`.
6. Контроли: device/APK mismatch и corrupted per-run evidence остаются fail-closed; валидный cycle по-прежнему resume/aggregate/validate/package проходить может.
7. Аналоги: перед выводом разобрать `build_s1_aggregate_from_disk` и `cmd_package` fallback с raw logs. Ни одна ошибка, влияющая на обязательный вход принятия, не должна пропасть между runner и завершающим валидатором.

**Условие принятия этого инженерного среза:** regression evidence для сценариев 1–6 на точном harness commit показывает: invalid attempt journal даёт nonzero exit до device/case operation и остаётся байт-в-байт неизменным; invalid cycle JSON даёт nonzero exit до device/case operation, сам файл остаётся неизменным, существующие attempt records сохраняются как prefix и добавляется ровно одна запись `FAILED`; valid control сохраняет прежние attempts и проходит существующие aggregate/package validation checks. Полный host suite запускается один раз на передаваемом commit. Продуктовые gate/task/CAP статусы не меняются. Это не закрывает B1/B2: дополнительно обязательны полный field/file/command inventory, reviewer и новый DEV run по §7.

## 1.2 Candidate audit — S1 instrumentation completion result (2026-09-28)

Scope: Gate B1/B2, I11/I21/I22, FROZEN Spike Protocol v1.1 §3.5 steps 5–11.
Source baseline `31375c63`, `host/runner.py` v1.6, SHA-256
`e527d6248190235b2b515f9609d8ef254be57a6ff717c0a2308789d9ea265bf4`; product
remains `.216` / code 335. This was initially a source-derived finding. Its
corrected Android result interpretation is in plan revision 5.360; implementation
and current verification are recorded in plan revision 5.361 and the checksummed
bundle `execution/device_tests/ENG-RUNNER-INSTRUMENTATION-EXIT-01/`.

**User result:** after an injected process death, S1 must observe a successful
read-only snapshot and successful aggregate before the host can accept the run.
FROZEN §3.5 requires restarting the app, capturing the snapshot and verifying the
oracle. ADB/instrumentation failure cannot substitute for that result. The
`start_case` instrumentation command is a distinct intentional-kill operation:
its nonzero result may be expected only when the run-specific `KILL_INJECT` marker,
PID termination check and subsequent snapshot/evidence checks all succeed.

**Class-wide command-result inventory in `host/runner.py`:**

| Site | Command / completion signal | Source audit | Disposition |
|---|---|---|---|
| `_execute_single_s1_case`, `res_snap` (~441–443) | `am instrument ... action snapshot`; accepts stdout containing `OK (` OR `INSTRUMENTATION_CODE: -1`, while omitting `returncode` | Snapshot action does not intentionally kill its instrumentation process (`S1Harness.runStep`, `S1Harness.java` snapshot branch). Android `-1` is `Activity.RESULT_OK`, not failure; accepting that marker alone can count runner-level success when the expected test did not run. A nonzero adb exit plus success-like text is also unexamined. | **Finding:** require adb return code 0 and exactly `OK (1 test)`; if a final instrumentation code is present it must be `-1`; reject failure/abort markers. Allow `-1` with the expected test summary. |
| `_run_s1_host_orchestrated`, `res_agg` (~644–647) | `am instrument ... action aggregate`; accepts `OK (` OR `INSTRUMENTATION_CODE: -1`, while omitting `returncode` | Aggregate action does not intentionally kill its instrumentation process; the same runner-level marker and adb-status gap applies. | **Same finding:** require adb return code 0 and exactly `OK (1 test)`; if a final instrumentation code is present it must be `-1`; reject failure/abort markers. Allow `-1` with the expected test summary. |
| `_execute_single_s1_case`, `res_case` (~394–418) | `start_case` intentionally kills the app process at the named hook | Not a success-text-only path: requires matching barrier + run_id + PID, checks `/proc/<pid>` is gone, then requires snapshot and pulled evidence | Protected special case; preserve the intended process-death behavior |
| `_execute_single_s1_case`, `proc_check` and retry (~423–434) | shell checks `/proc/<pid>` | Return code is checked and only exact `PROCESS_GONE` is accepted | Protected |
| `_run_instrumented` (~275–281), `cmd_run_all` S2–S6 (~733–737) | S2–S6 instrumentation | Both check nonzero exit, `OK (` and absence of `FAILURES!!!` | Protected analogs; retain regression coverage |
| `cmd_audit`, `measure_device_metadata`, resume identity/hash queries, required pulls | ADB state/metadata/hash/file reads | Return code and/or exact output, existence, length or later checksum/schema validation is required | Protected by source checks; broader field-level mapping remains open |
| `check_file` (~446–448), `cmd_package` raw-log copy (~2920–2930), optional device-log pull (~484–490, 654) | Success marker / best-effort copies | Per-run required evidence is still pulled and `raw_log_location` is checked against packaged bytes; the optional device-log copy is not the authoritative S1 raw host transcript | Not the same false-success path; include in remaining I07/I21/I22 inventory |
| `logcat -c`, failure-path logcat capture, force-stop, pre-run `rm -rf`, extra `logcat_ALL` capture, PM permission grants | Reset/hygiene/diagnostics | Distinct from successful snapshot/aggregate; each has downstream run-identity, process, required-evidence or instrumentation checks, or is supplemental telemetry | Keep recorded as command analogs; do not infer these establish a complete I21 inventory |

The two candidate false-acceptance sites are the only S1 normal snapshot/aggregate
completion paths in this class that accept a runner-level `INSTRUMENTATION_CODE`
marker without requiring the targeted test result and without checking adb's
return code. Android defines `Activity.RESULT_OK` as `-1`; Android's test-result
parser also treats final `INSTRUMENTATION_CODE: -1` as instrumentation success,
including when no tests ran. Therefore `-1` must remain allowed with the expected
one-test summary, and must not substitute for that summary. See [Android
Activity.RESULT_OK](https://developer.android.com/reference/android/app/Activity#RESULT_OK)
and the [Android instrumentation result parser tests](https://android.googlesource.com/platform/tools/base/+/088f74c4fa52d08871b31635be96ab8ae05c87bb%5E!/).
The intentional `start_case` call is excluded: it kills the app process by design,
and its acceptance remains based on the run-specific marker, PID, observed process
death, then valid snapshot/evidence. This list does not close the wider I21
inventory across commands, fields or S2–S6.

**Required positive/negative controls before the fix:**

1. Positive S1 run/snapshot and aggregate controls still complete using normal
   zero-exit `OK` output and preserve existing evidence.
2. Snapshot returns nonzero with `OK (1 test)`; runner exits before treating the
   per-run JSON/evidence as a successful snapshot.
3. Snapshot returns zero with only `INSTRUMENTATION_CODE: -1` and no one-test summary; runner fails closed. With `OK (1 test)` plus `INSTRUMENTATION_CODE: -1`, the runner accepts the successful Android result.
4. Aggregate returns nonzero with `OK (1 test)`; runner fails before final success.
5. Aggregate returns zero with only `INSTRUMENTATION_CODE: -1` and no one-test summary; runner fails closed. With `OK (1 test)` plus `INSTRUMENTATION_CODE: -1`, the runner accepts the successful Android result.
6. `OK (0 tests)`, any final instrumentation result code other than `-1`, `INSTRUMENTATION_FAILED`, or `INSTRUMENTATION_ABORTED` never counts as the expected test. `OK (1 test)` with nonzero adb return code also fails closed.
7. Intentional `start_case` process death remains accepted only with its unique
   marker, PID termination, successful snapshot and valid evidence; unrelated
   S2–S6 tests continue checking nonzero exit.

**Acceptance condition:** addressed negative tests fail at the corresponding
snapshot/aggregate boundary and prevent later success-dependent commands; positive
controls accept `OK (1 test)` with zero adb status and optional
`INSTRUMENTATION_CODE: -1`; the intentional process-death control remains valid.
Focused orchestrator tests and one complete host/build/traceability/task-ledger/
evidence check pass on the final source; raw logs/checksums are stored. Increment
runner version 1.6 → 1.7. No app version, frozen threshold, gate, task or CAP
status changes. B1/B2 still require the complete I01–I25 field/file/command
inventory, independent reviewer and a new DEV run under §7.

**Engineering result (2026-09-28):** runner v1.7 commit `fa4d7ad2`, SHA-256
`95b75edd16df18fc7ef939a79dc8202c319ae70d84d7fbd44ccc5162f97dcbab`; focused
controls 3/3, orchestrator suite 22/22, configured `check_all.sh --rerun` exit 0
(Gradle 123 tasks; host 107/107; traceability/task ledger/non-strict B0 evidence
validation passed). Exact outputs and checksums are under
`execution/device_tests/ENG-RUNNER-INSTRUMENTATION-EXIT-01/`. No device was
connected: instrumentation and DEV were NOT RUN. This closes the host-only
engineering slice only; B1/B2 remain IN_PROGRESS and REVIEW_REQUIRED.

## 1. Обязательный порядок ревью

1. До ревью нового runner обновить этот документ по frozen-протоколу, схемам,
   producer-коду Android, host-коду и реальным пакетам. Diff — только указатель изменений.
2. Для каждого поля, вложенного поля, файла и внешней операции проверить:
   **P** Presence, **F** Format, **C** Cross-check, **E** Failure propagation.
3. Найденный дефект классифицировать по P/F/C/E. Выполнить поиск того же паттерна
   по ВСЕМУ `host/runner.py`, затем по связанным validator/producer-контрактам.
   В одном отчёте перечислить все найденные места, включая защищённые аналоги.
4. До реализации фикса передать Gravity полный набор негативных случаев для
   затронутого класса инвариантов. Фикс должен покрывать класс, а не одну строку.
5. Принимать по исходникам, исполненным регрессионным тестам и новому DEV-циклу.
   Не считать число зелёных тестов доказательством полноты.

`if x:`, `.get(..., 0)`, `except`, `check=False` сами по себе не дефекты.
Для каждого места необходимо доказать обязательность значения, разрешённый fallback
или обязательную последующую обработку ошибки. Поиск — инвентаризация рисков,
не автоматическое доказательство обхода.

## 2. Формат полного реестра

Каждая строка итогового реестра соответствует ОДНОМУ конкретному JSON path,
файловому контракту либо внешней операции. Группы ниже — начальная карта scope,
НЕ замена поэлементной инвентаризации и НЕ основание заявить 100% покрытия.

Обязательные колонки для развёрнутых строк:

`ID | source/section | artifact + JSON path | spike/mode/condition | P | F | C | E | code commit:path:line/symbol | test ID for each property | execution/evidence | reviewer verdict`

Для P/F/C/E допустимы `TODO`, `PASS`, `FAIL`, `N/A:обоснование`.
PASS требует проверенного кода и исполненного теста. Для условного поля явно
описать условие обязательности и протестировать обе ветви. Nullable telemetry
требует причины unavailable/censored и не может подменять наблюдение нулём.
Копии одного утверждения в двух JSON не являются независимым измерением.

## 5. Матрица adversarial-тестов для Gravity — до реализации

Для КАЖДОГО обязательного поля из полного реестра параметризовать:

- **T-P:** удалить; null; пустая строка/whitespace; пустой контейнер; строка `null`.
- **T-F:** неправильный scalar/container, bool вместо number, NaN/Infinity,
  отрицательное/дробное значение счётчика, unknown enum, повреждённый формат hash.
- **T-C:** заменить только один источник; оба JSON согласованы, но диск/fixture
  отличается; foreign run/operation/device; duplicate ID; переставить порядок файлов.
- **T-E:** сбой чтения/hash/renderer/ADB; timeout; nonzero с правдоподобным stdout;
  отсутствие файла при returncode=0; ожидаемая остановка до зависимого шага.
- **T-ROUNDTRIP:** полный положительный fixture, мутация, package/relocate/validate,
  resume и повторный resume. Обязателен контроль отсутствия побочных действий после отказа.

Для optional/условных полей тестировать допустимое отсутствие и его границу.
Невалидный пакет может возвращать validation error, наблюдённое нарушение — FAIL,
отсутствие доказательства — INCOMPLETE; ни одно из них не даёт успешную приёмку gate.
Успешная проверка формата FAIL/INCOMPLETE-пакета не равна успешному experimental outcome.
Каждый тест должен ломать именно целевой инвариант на иначе корректном fixture;
отказ по другой причине не подтверждает защиту. Mock не должен подменять проверяемый код.

## 6. Формулировка следующего requests-to-fix

> Валидатор нигде не должен принимать PASS при отсутствии обязательного поля
> сравнения, обязательного файла или результата наблюдения. Инвентаризировать
> каждый такой operand в runner.py и связанных валидаторах. Для каждого указать
> P/F/C/E, code location и negative test. Найденный класс распространить на все
> применимые места в одном согласованном исправлении; исключения обосновать.
> Не менять frozen outcomes, не ослаблять tests, не объявлять неизвестное нулём.

Форма отчёта одной находки:
`ID → P/F/C/E → воспроизведение → ВСЕ аналогичные места → исключения → tests → fix/evidence → verdict`.

## 7. Условия закрытия B1/B2

- Полный field/file/command inventory выведен из нормативных источников И producer/schema/code.
- Включены вложенные paths и conditional поля; все группы разделены на отдельные строки.
- Нет полей без классификации и нет TODO. Для N/A есть согласованное обоснование.
- Для каждой применимой P/F/C/E проверки есть code reference и исполненный regression test.
- Проведён сквозной поиск аналогичных паттернов; ни один найденный участок не оставлен без решения.
- Новый DEV-прогон соответствует проверенному APK/code commit; raw evidence и package валидны.
- Независимый reviewer подтвердил матрицу и результат. Самооценка Gravity не заменяет review.

Покрытие считать отдельно: inventory completeness, tests mapped, tests executed,
reviewed PASS. Знаменатель — полный подтверждённый inventory; до его завершения
процент покрытия **не определён**, не 100%. S5/S6 не исключать молча из общего B1.

На момент создания документа B1/B2 остаются **IN_PROGRESS по новой методологии**.
Исторические DEV-пакеты и локальные приёмки сохраняются; новые дефекты ими не
предполагаются. Это изменение критерия полной приёмки, а не отмена измерений.

### 11.2 External command and file-operation inventory — source pass

An AST walk of the tested `host/runner.py` v1.7 source (`fa4d7ad2`) found 48
`run_cmd` call sites: 31 use `check=False`, 3 explicitly use `check=True`, and
14 inherit `run_cmd`'s strict default. All run through its 60-second timeout;
timeout is represented as exit 124 (strict callers exit; non-strict callers
must inspect the result). This table records all non-strict call-site groups;
the three strict final S1 pulls and strict-default calls are protected by
`run_cmd` exit handling, but downstream file/schema checks still apply.

| Call site(s) in `host/runner.py` | Operation / consumer | Existing guard or evidence | Inventory finding / required disposition |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cmd_audit:203` | `adb get-state` | Checks return code and exact `device` output. | Protected for the state assertion. No command mutation test is mapped. |
| `cmd_install:264–265` | Grant CAMERA to app and test APK | APK installs are strict; grants are not inspected; command prints installed afterward. | Result is not independently verified. Map `install` result vs later instrumentation and define failure propagation as part of command batch. |
| `_run_instrumented:277` | Single S2–S6 instrumentation invocation | Checks rc, presence of substring `OK (`, and absence of `FAILURES!!!`. | **Source-level false-acceptance candidate:** `OK (0 tests)` and a wrong nonzero test count satisfy the textual predicate. No mutation regression mapped. |
| `_run_instrumented:308` | Logcat after instrumentation | Explicitly checks return code before writing log. | Protected for this capture. `run_cmd` error and timeout tests cover the generic wrapper, not the capture callsite. |
| `record_failure_and_exit:394` | Best-effort diagnostic logcat when an S1 case fails | Its stdout is included in failure log; return code/stderr are ignored. | Diagnostic-only fallback; logcat failure can leave empty diagnostics. Must remain a failed run and be recorded distinctly; no injected capture-failure test mapped. |
| `_execute_single_s1_case:415` | Clear logcat before a new run | Return code ignored. | Precondition result is not proven. Include cleanup/clear failure and stale-log isolation in batch. |
| `_execute_single_s1_case:419` | `start_case` instrumentation intentionally kills app | Its rc is not the oracle; exact run-specific `KILL_INJECT` marker, PID and `/proc` death are required. | Intentional exception; preserve. Existing process-death and host-orchestration controls cover portions; marker/PID collision and command-output mutation remain to map. |

The remaining strict/default `run_cmd` sites are also inventoried: APK build
(`cmd_build:237`), app/test installs (`cmd_install:262–263`), start cleanup,
logcat clear and evidence pull (`_run_instrumented:270,273,316`), device
property reads (`cmd_audit:209–214`), and cycle evidence/log pulls
(`cmd_run_all:772,777`). APK existence/hash operations at `cmd_build:242–247`
are host filesystem checks, not `run_cmd` sites. Strict/default subprocesses
use generic runner exit handling; property emptiness and local file-presence
conditions are checked separately and are not inferred from rc=0.

The source walk also identified these host filesystem boundaries in the same
finite set: JSON/hash reads of `configs/frozen_hashes.json`, manifests, every
cycle JSON, `resume_attempts.json`, and gate ledgers; writing cycle manifests,
host/device transcripts, resume journals, aggregate JSON, package manifest,
report and checksum file; per-run evidence and final subtree pulls; raw/log/dump/
artifact copy into package; package-wide SHA-256 generation/verification;
and cleanup with `shutil.rmtree(target_dir)` in `cmd_package`. `_safe_package_path`
is used for per-run log references and checks traversal/symlink escape. Resume
journal corruption is preserved and rejected by `_load_resume_attempts`; its
existing corruption/malformed-history tests are reusable.

Source-level package findings against `docs/05_RESULTS_PACKAGE_CONTRACT.md`:

1. `cmd_package` constructs `spikes_included` as all six S1–S6 regardless of
   whether each aggregate was found/copied. `validate_dir` classifies and
   validates aggregates that exist but has no all-six set assertion. The frozen
   package contract requires all six aggregates. Existing checksum round-trip
   positive fixture intentionally contains only a DEV S1 declaration; preserve
   that standalone/subset validation use and put the all-six rule on final
   qualification-package creation/validation only.
2. `qualification-manifest.json` currently contains only `manifest_version`,
   `execution_mode`, `dut_id`, `app_package`, `generated_at`, `source_cycle`,
   `hard_power_extension_executed`, `frozen_hashes_verified`, and
   `spikes_included`. Contract 05 additionally requires exact manufacturer,
   model, SKU, Android/API/fingerprint/security patch/kernel/filesystem/ABI/
   MemTotal, app version/build hash, host runner revision/hash and execution
   start/end. Those exact manifest paths have no producer, validator or mutation
   test mapping yet. Do not synthesize physical fields from a DEV emulator.
3. `frozen_hashes_verified` is written as a Boolean result, but `cmd_package`
   does not stop if it is false and `validate_dir` does not enforce it. `verify-gates`
   independently checks hashes; map which final-package entry point is required
   to reject mismatch before assigning the final verdict.
4. `cmd_package` deletes an existing target with `shutil.rmtree` before copying
   or validating, and does not reject a source/target alias. A copy, hash or
   validation failure can therefore destroy the previously usable package; a
   source-target alias can erase the source tree. This is a source-level
   destructive-boundary finding; no command was run against output paths and no
   data loss was reproduced. The package contract does not state overwrite
   semantics; retain the currently delivered package until staged output has
   passed validation, then replace atomically, and reject aliases.
5. `cmd_verify_gates` uses `.get("gates", {})` and `.get("tasks", [])` and can
   iterate empty collections; the on-disk `execution/tasks.json` has 12 gates
   and 11 tasks, while `execution/product_tasks.json` is the separate product
   ledger. The route must remain explicit about which ledger is normative for
   this harness subcommand. No mutation test for missing/wrong/empty container
   shape is mapped. This candidate concerns schema rejection; it does not
   authorize status changes.
6. During `cmd_package` raw-log repair, `raw_log_location` is joined to both
   source and target without `_safe_package_path`; `mkdir`/`copy2` may therefore
   touch a path outside the package before the later `validate_dir` rejects the
   reference. This is a source-level path-boundary candidate only: it has not
   been executed or reproduced. Add traversal, absolute-path, and symlink
   controls that assert no outside-tree mutation and preserve the input cycle.

the commands and files actually prove. The list is finite for the audited

each candidate against DEV and QUALIFICATION conditions; the implementation
batch is now ready under the unchanged active-package contract. Exact targets,
evidence bounds and residual actions are in §11.19.

still NOT RUN for the newly listed cells. Existing checks and evidence above

#### 11.5.2 S1 read-only state oracle and cross-file binding — revision 5.381

Protocol §3.5 requires the host to inspect pre-recovery bytes, ArtifactRecord,
every ArtifactReference, and the owning entity. The finite barrier conditions
are D1–D4 (no authoritative reference; artifact survival not required), D5
(exact bytes if publication success returned), D6 (exact bytes plus
`STAGED_DURABLE`, no reference), D7 (wholly uncommitted or wholly committed),
and D8 (exact bytes, `COMMITTED` record, reference and owning row together).
This is the normative minimum; individual Android database columns beyond the
state and identity needed for that oracle remain producer-detail until mapped
to a frozen claim.

#### 11.5.3 Diagnostic database open must not create or migrate — revision 5.395

Frozen Protocol v1.1 §3.5 calls for exporting the read-only diagnostic state
after process death and before recovery mutation. Source inspection found that
`S1Diagnostic.capture` uses `new S1Database(context).getReadableDatabase()`.
Although `S1Database.onOpen` is neutral, `SQLiteOpenHelper` owns create/upgrade
callbacks; Android's API documents `getReadableDatabase()` as “Create and/or
open a database.” An absent DB may therefore be changed into an empty database
and then look like an empty observation. This is an in-scope implementation
omission in the frozen read-only requirement, not a new acceptance criterion.

Before code changes, the required fix and test are preregistered in plan
revision 5.395: open only the already-existing DB with
`SQLiteDatabase.OPEN_READONLY`; propagate absent, inaccessible, corrupt, and
query failures; prove an absent file remains absent; and prove a readable v1
schema is not upgraded by capture. Existing fully provisioned DB tables with
no matching rows remain a valid empty-state observation. The isolated
instrumentation result will be attached to `S1-STATE-ORACLE-01`; it cannot close
physical qualification or imply a process-death device result.


Execution result (plan revision 5.396): S1Diagnostic.capture now uses the
explicit read-only open and propagates failures. Attempt 24 passed
s1DiagnosticCaptureDoesNotCreateOrUpgradeDatabase (1/1) on
DocScanMvpTest_API_36.1; it observed that an absent file remained absent, a
provisioned empty database remained empty, and user_version=1 was unchanged.
Attempt 26 passed s1DiagnosticDatabaseReadFailureDoesNotBecomeEmptyState
(1/1) on the same AVD; missing-table queries raised and provisioned empty-table
queries returned null/empty. Attempt 25 passed 251 S1/run-schema/S6/audit
pytest tests and 106 validator/orchestrator/S5 unittest tests; static checks
passed. Raw commands and outputs are under attempts 23–26 in
execution/device_tests/ENG-B1B2-INVENTORY-01/.

This closes the read-only-open correction at the focused host/harness boundary.
It does not provide the final candidate's full S1 D1–D8 DEV run (100 repeats
per barrier), physical qualification, independent review or owner acceptance.

Static gaps that remain within the same I23 class:

- `_validate_resume_attempts_data` requires `attempt_timestamp`, `spike`,
  `mode`, `serial`, and `outcome`, but validates only mode, outcome enum, and
  emulator/canonical-serial conditions. It does not parse timestamp, close the
  spike enum against the resumed spike, require a nonblank typed serial, or
  validate `executed_runs`/run IDs or relation to earlier attempts. QUAL
  history is loaded without a canonical serial argument (`runner.py:839–850`,
  `2659–2662`), so its serial comparison does not bind each prior attempt to
  the cycle serial at that point.
- `cmd_resume` accumulates fingerprint/hash/serial fields across JSON files
  until the first truthy tuple is complete. This can combine identity from
  different files. After that tuple becomes complete, later files are still
  parsed for corruption but their identity fields are not compared. `dut_id`
  is captured in `cycle_dut_id` but is not consumed. `cycle_mode` is checked
  only when present/truthy (`runner.py:2663–2702`, `2754–2767`). The effective
  mismatch test covers cycle serial versus device serial; no valid executed
  cycle APK-hash mismatch control was found, and no all-file identity
  cross-binding/order permutations are tested.
- Device fingerprint and `sha256sum` commands require rc 0 and nonempty output;
  `pm path` accepts any output containing a `package:` line without checking
  return code (`runner.py:2734–2752`). The parsed APK digest token is compared
  with the cycle value but is not independently required to be 64 lowercase
  hex (`2758–2764`). Existing tests cover missing fingerprint/hash-query and
  serial mismatch, not a valid cycle APK-hash mismatch, plausible package
  output with nonzero rc, or malformed matching digest tokens.
- The journal mutation controls cover root type, required-key omission,
  outcome enum, emulator serial, and unreadable-file preservation. They do not
  cover timestamp/spike/serial/`executed_runs` field types, blank/null values,
  duplicate run IDs across attempts, preservation of earlier records during a
  successful append/update, or new-attempt ID/reference linkage required by
  `docs/08_MVP_GATES_AND_ACCEPTANCE.md:51`.

the existing positive end-to-end and non-destructive history cases; add a

each journal field's type/value; seed repeated/mislinked `executed_runs`; and
make each ADB preflight mock return nonzero rc alongside plausible stdout.
Acceptance requires failure before any S1 execution on every mismatch, source
evidence preservation, and a truthful append/update that preserves prior
attempt records. Check that attempted writes do not drop or rewrite older
entries; this does not add a tamper-evident history requirement. Retain S2
rejection, ordinary missing-command failures, and exact identity comparison
as controls. No new retry or qualification scope is added.

No tests or device commands were run during this inventory refinement. The

### 11.8 Gate/task input and verdict links — I25

There are two separate ledgers by design. `execution/tasks.json` is the harness
subcommand input read by `host/runner.py::cmd_verify_gates`; it currently contains
12 gates and 11 harness tasks. `execution/product_tasks.json` is the product
MVP ledger and is read by its own validator through `tools/check_all.sh`, not by
`cmd_verify_gates`. `execution/traceability.csv` is the harness traceability
input; product `execution/traceability_product.csv` is separately validated.
This separation is not itself a conflict or permission to merge/status-edit the
ledgers.

#### 11.9.3 I14–I20 state-dump schema and run binding — revision 5.381

Frozen Protocol §9 requires `pre_state_dump` and `post_state_dump` in every
S1–S6 per-run record and represents each as `null` in the schema template.
S1 also has standalone dumps and the stronger D1–D8 state oracle in §§3–3.5;
S5/S6 have their explicit nested state roots in §11.9.1. S2–S4 have no frozen
nested child schema beyond §9, so their existing `{}` producer values are
valid empty diagnostics and must not be expanded into new state requirements.

For S1, standalone dumps independently exist as files but still originate from
the app snapshot. The current reader cross-check is limited to five embedded
values and does not bind external SHA-256 or state entities; see §11.5.2. For
S2, `pages[]` is producer extension and its missing top-level state keys
already pass an executed INCOMPLETE fixture. S3/S4 empty objects occur in
executed positive fixtures. This source/log audit has no physical device or
QUALIFICATION dump proof.

**Batch condition `RUN-STATE-SCHEMA-01`:** one positive per spike with both
schema keys represented as null or valid object according to the frozen
template/producer; one-at-a-time missing and wrong-type mutations for the
top-level keys; preserve S1 D1–D8 state semantics, S5/S6 conditional state
validators, and S2's current checks. If `pages[]` remains emitted, mutations
must not be accepted as false committed-page evidence; do not mandate extra
member fields without a frozen requirement. Retain standalone dump path,
timestamp, run/type and artifact-byte controls. Require no new S3/S4 nested
data or measurement threshold.

**Consolidated regression contract candidate `I13-QUAL-MATRIX-01`:**

- For every spike, build a complete qualification fixture at precisely the
  frozen matrix size and require it to validate; then remove one required cell,
  misassign one run to another workload/fixture/point/scenario/tuple/hook, and
  add one out-of-matrix run. Each invalid fixture must fail qualification.
- S2: preserve workload batch identity and prove 20 × 100 commands per
  workload, with each accepted `operation_id` tied through C1–C7 and explicit
  typed failure accounting for any non-accepted command.
- S3: bind 20 distinct 50-run batches per fixture, restart the app between
  batches, and prove all 1,000 runs; separately prove 500 contention sets and
  their admission observations.
- S4: require exactly 50 runs at each point and exactly 200 distinct P_MAX

### 11.13 Common per-run schema — top-level enforcement and identity (I01–I11, I21–I22)

Frozen Protocol v1.1 §9 (lines 1185–1207) defines 17 top-level paths for every
S1–S6 run record. `host/runner.py:1100–1110` has a shared presence list with 13
keys: the 12 listed below plus implementation field `execution_mode`. It only
adds `injection_hook`, `pre_state_dump`, and `post_state_dump` for S1. Current
source does not put `kill_condition_triggered` or `notes` in the common list.
The other three §9 paths are therefore not required by the shared path for
S2–S6; S6 uses separate `dump1/2/3_*` members. Missing-key source candidate.

| Frozen path / property | Current behavior and existing evidence | Remaining P/F/C/E control |
|---|---|---|
| `spike_id`, `case_id`, `injection_hook` | Presence is checked for `spike_id`/`case_id`; `spike_id` dispatches validators. S1 exact case↔hook is checked (`runner.py:1150–1154`), S2 case enum is closed (`1155–1158`), and S6 checks hook enum (`1797–1808`). S3 fixture and S5 scenario IDs are counted by their aggregate path; S5 per-run loop does not reject an unrecognized case ID, and no common hook/fixture registry is applied. Existing tests include `test_s2_invalid_case_id`, `test_reject_incompatible_case_id_and_injection_hook`, `test_s6_validator_rejects_unknown_hook_enum`; the S6 pytest-style test is not collected by check-all. | Enumerate every allowed spike/case/hook and conditional association from the frozen protocol; reject unknown/extra IDs and hook mismatch for S3–S5, with valid null/unused representation only when the protocol permits it. Preserve intentional S1/S6 hook semantics. |
| `run_id`, `operation_id` | `run_id` must be truthy and unique (`runner.py:1025–1035`); no common string/type/format check. `operation_id` key presence is required, but there is no common nonempty/type/uniqueness check. S1 uses it as the `.bin` filename (`1215–1217`); S2's operation-to-C1…C7 binding is not established by this field check. Existing coverage includes missing QUAL `run_id` and `test_reject_duplicate_run_id`. | Bind run and operation identity to their producer command/event and referenced artifacts; test null/blank, wrong JSON type, duplicate or foreign operation identity and mismatched filename/content. Do not invent an ID regex absent producer/frozen rule. |
| `device_build_fingerprint`, `app_build_hash`, `execution_mode` | Required by key presence; mode is checked against selected validator mode (`runner.py:1037–1043`). QUAL serial/DUT/model checks and fingerprint/hash tuple equality are conditional on truthy values (`1050–1093`), so empty strings bypass that equality branch. `execution_mode` is an implementation-required field absent from §9's 17-key example; the cycle manifest requires mode (`runner.py:948–958`) and Contract 05 requires aggregate mode (`docs/05_RESULTS_PACKAGE_CONTRACT.md:57–64`), but those do not explicitly specify a per-run mode member. | Require authoritative nonempty typed identity in QUAL and cross-bind manifest, per-run, dump, aggregate, installed APK/source and serial. Keep the existing per-run mode guard; map its provenance through actual producers and package contract before changing it. Do not treat it as a frozen §9 path. |
| `start_monotonic_ns`, `end_monotonic_ns` | Both must be positive strict integers, with end ≥ start (`runner.py:1112–1120`). Existing named controls include `test_reject_per_run_zero_start_monotonic_ns`; the broader timestamp test inventory does not yet establish both common fields across all spike types. | Add false/zero/fraction/string/reversed and cross-run epoch/order cases for both fields; confirm source clock and units without adding a performance threshold. |
| `measured_metrics` | Key presence is common; the common path does not require an object. S1/S2 and selected later spike branches read selected members, but no common shape exists. For S3, aggregate counts are not derived from this object in the inspected branch. | Type each metric object from its frozen per-spike map; missing/null/wrong-type value and aggregate/per-run disagreement mutations across S1–S6. |
| `artifact_checks` | Key presence is common; no shared list/element schema. S2 derives `check_names` from dict entries and requires two named checks (`runner.py:1163–1170`). Generic PASS contradiction code only inspects it when it is a list (`1369–1375`), so a non-list can bypass that generic scan. | Require the frozen list/object shape and closed check registry per spike; missing, duplicate, unknown, wrong-type and false checks must reconcile with aggregate outcome/exit status. Preserve the S1 intentional process-death result. |
| `raw_log_location` | Requires nonempty string, safe in-package path, existing nonempty regular file (`runner.py:1122–1129`). Existing tests cover traversal, missing file and null location. No generic binding of log contents to run/operation/hook/PID is performed by this check. | Reuse path-safety tests; add same-size foreign/stale log, wrong run/operation/hook/PID and overwritten-transcript evidence controls. Keep device transcript distinct from authoritative host result. |
| `pre_state_dump`, `post_state_dump` | Both are required nonempty objects only for S1 (`runner.py:1105–1106`, `1134–1143`); no explicit-null presence check for other spikes. S6's separate diagnostics do not enforce these §9 keys. | Require the two members for every run; use nonempty typed objects for applicable hooks and explicit schema-allowed null when inapplicable. Cross-bind applicable dumps to external files and run identity. |
| `kill_condition_triggered`, `notes` | Neither is in the shared required list. Generic aggregate-PASS contradiction handling accepts absence and only treats nonempty lists or selected strings (`"violation"`, `"fail"`, `"error"`) as a kill; booleans and other strings are not consistently typed (`runner.py:1362–1369`). S6 later requires kill hook equality; S1 intentionally triggers process death. The executed S4 DEV PASS fixture in `test_s4_aggregate_and_host_pdf_validation` omits both paths and passes in retained host log lines 283–288. | Define frozen per-spike null/value semantics, require presence and type, test false/true/list/string/null and unknown diagnostics, and reconcile each violation with run/aggregate/outcome. Do not classify expected S1/S6 injected deaths as product failures. `notes` remains nullable as the template shows; its type must be derived from producers. |

Additional observed positive-fixture omission: executed unittest
`test_s2_valid_dev_evidence` passes with a DEV `INCOMPLETE` aggregate while its

by `tools/check_all.sh`; do not call that execution evidence.

**Consolidated regression contract candidate `COMMON-RUN-SCHEMA-01`:**

- Positive control: one valid per-run record for each S1–S6, with all 17 frozen
  members, correct conditional null/objects, identity bindings, and matching
  aggregate; include separate DEV and QUAL fixtures so DEV cannot satisfy QUAL.
- Negative set: remove each top-level member individually; substitute null,
  wrong JSON type, empty identity, unknown enum, foreign operation/log/dump,
  malformed `artifact_checks`, and contradictory kill/outcome values. For every
  applicable field, verify both per-run rejection and the package-level result.
- Reuse existing missing/duplicate run ID, timestamp, safe-log, dump-identity,
  S1 hook, S2 case/check and S6 enum controls; close the named untested cells
  rather than duplicating already-proven behavior.
- Trace the extra per-run `execution_mode` member to actual producer
  serialization and the package-level mode contract; retain the current guard
  while this mapping is open. Keep `outcome` classified as a runner extension
  because it is absent from §9's per-run template.

No test/build/ADB/package/device command was run for this source mapping.
Candidate regression tests remain inside the existing consolidated I01–I25

**Cross-cutting preservation oracle:** every field mutation must begin from a
fully valid aggregate/per-run package for the same mode. A malformed independent
field must produce the contract's intended outcome/diagnostic, must not be
masked by an earlier unrelated failure, and must preserve raw source evidence.
Use strict JSON type distinctions (`bool` is not an integer count), closed
enums, and finite nonnegative values where the frozen field is a measurement;
do not add latency or accuracy thresholds. Separate `PASS` kill-counter
requirements from typed operation failures, missing required work, and
qualification-incomplete results.

**Resolved outcome interpretation `ENG-AGGREGATE-OUTCOME-01`:** Protocol §2.5
defines `FAIL` by the per-spike kill-condition lists and `INCOMPLETE` by missing
mandatory work/result/evidence. Therefore a typed operation failure or
implementation-only extension counter is not independently a kill; preserve it
and reconcile it to run evidence. A run with an identified typed failure can
coexist with aggregate `PASS` only when the mandatory work and evidence are
complete and no frozen kill is present. An unclassified/undetectable operation
result makes the aggregate `INCOMPLETE`. Apply the same rule to S1's
`failed_runs_count`/`oracle_violations*` extensions and the generic per-run
`outcome` / `artifact_checks` contradiction loop. S2 and S4 examples are explicit
in `execution/decisions.md`; this is a protocol-derived interpretation, not a
new outcome or threshold. Source deltas are concrete: S1's disk aggregator makes
any non-PASS run and any false artifact check a FAIL input; S2's producer also
treats typed failures, accepted/committed mismatch, failed health observation,
background error and unconfirmed permit overlap as kill inputs. S4 now records
per-run typed failures and validates committed outputs by explicit source status;
attempt 57 proves a complete typed-only failure can coexist with aggregate PASS.
Remaining spike-specific outcome cells stay in I12. In the regression contract,
only frozen kill conditions may yield FAIL; a typed failure with complete
evidence is counted, while incomplete observation/reconciliation is INCOMPLETE.

### S2 aggregate latency source row — attempt 62 preregistration (plan 5.434)

The 18 frozen workload fields are the six `request_to_tx_commit_ms_{p50,p95,p99}` / `request_to_page_visible_ms_{p50,p95,p99}` values for each C-W0/C-W1/C-W2. Producer source is `S2Harness.executeWorkload`: successful capture rows store integer elapsed milliseconds; those exact observations feed the aggregate lists. `request_to_tx_commit_ms` is computed as `(tTxCommitNs-tIntakeNs)/1_000_000`, but the separate transaction timestamp is not serialized. `request_to_page_visible_ms` can be independently recomputed from successful-row `end_monotonic_ns-start_monotonic_ns`, since these endpoints are intake and page-visible time. Host validation currently checks only aggregate numeric shape and does not recompute from retained successful rows.

A missing row or invalid source remains an evidence failure. Exact DEV and QUAL matrix sizes are unchanged; QUAL remains 20×100 rows per workload. No latency SLA is added. Preregistered controls, source limits, evidence path and completion condition are in plan revisions 5.434–5.435.

# Model and runtime provenance

DocAligner source: DOCSAID Lab, repository
https://github.com/DocsaidLab/DocAligner, pinned revision
`3275b0f07f8e99d8c01cb0774dea2549be1416b6`. The independent AndroidTest
translation follows `docaligner/heatmap_reg/infer.py` preprocessing and
postprocessing. Source license: [Apache-2.0](licenses/DocAligner-Apache-2.0.txt).
The source license is not asserted to establish rights to exact legacy weights.

| Candidate artifact | Bytes | SHA-256 | Location / distribution |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| LC100 legacy heatmap FP32 | 4767987 | f4117b786e3a18470f3865c93f3c2bd69d9b998edd60f385574a5c665e79594e | Optional local AndroidTest fixture; absent from production APK/Git |
| T8 legacy heatmap FP32 | 13167814 | 950070fd4a46e25d46db7c35d0ed77612d9063f70d4543c7c504f0da6a943a89 | Same |

Exact metadata and byte lengths: `runs/models-reference/reference-results.json`.
The explicit downloader verifies pinned SHA-256 and never runs from the app,
Gradle configuration or an ordinary build. Do not redistribute the optional test
models until the legacy artifacts' license scope is established. No vendor was
contacted and no commercial terms were accepted.

Android test runtime is `com.microsoft.onnxruntime:onnxruntime-android:1.23.2`
(MIT), AndroidTest configuration only. CPU FP32, two intra-op threads; no delegate,
quantization or claimed Android-wide numerical equivalence. Upstream host Python
versions and exact freeze are archived in `runs/models-reference/`.

Both models expose only `[1,4,128,128]` heatmaps from BGR CHW `/255` input. Their
reference adapters return AMBIGUOUS and retain raw candidates. The observed
non-document graphic-panel lock is retained as a counterexample; output shape
or reference parity does not demonstrate document presence.

# DBQ engine decision — provisional, 2026-10-20

**Selection verdict: INCONCLUSIVE. No qualified winner.** This record preserves
§22, including its prohibition on declaring a winner without comparable evidence.
Physical checks are scheduled after implementation by the owner's direction.

| Variant | Implemented / executed evidence | Qualification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Original 0.4.279 | Forced 184+48 unit tests; 3 native fixture tests on API36 emulator; fixed source commit e62a5b5 | Real camera quality and resources NOT_RUN |
| Original + common chain 0.4.280 | Forced 184+59 unit tests, signed APKs; deadline/callback/capture-policy regressions | Overlay instrumentation INCONCLUSIVE; hardware NOT_RUN |
| A + common chain | Bounded contour/rotation-independent line hypotheses, per-side gradient evidence and Huber refinement; runnable debug backend | Software native/refiner/tracker regressions PASS within 19-method emulator suite; real-corpus comparison NOT_RUN |
| B-LC100 FP32 CPU | Upstream host postprocess parity and Android test-only reference | Heatmap-only; observed non-document panel false lock; not eligible for production |
| B-T8 FP32 CPU | Same reference harness, exact pinned artifact | Same false lock; misses one generated paper found by LC100; not eligible for production |
| Tracker / filters / refinement ablations | Independently runnable components, prediction disabled | Camera jitter/lag and sufficient final corpus NOT_RUN |

Reference model evidence is in `runs/models-reference/`. Both legacy checkpoint
files have only four heatmap channels, without an object-presence head. Reference
adapters deliberately return AMBIGUOUS and expose raw points for comparison. Four
corners alone cannot authorize a confirmed outline or automatic crop.

The upstream code is Apache-2.0. The official catalog's broad weight-use wording
and the exact legacy Drive artifact hashes have not been explicitly linked by an
artifact license. Weights remain local optional AndroidTest fixtures, excluded
from Git and production APKs; ONNX Runtime 1.23.2 is AndroidTest-only. No vendor
messages, commercial agreements or network/GMS requirement were introduced.

Production uses the original detector behind the common timing/viewport/ownership
contract. A and tracker are explicit debug experiments, not an automatic fallback
whose scores are compared across engines. Prediction stays disabled because
preview presentation time has not been measured. JPEG still refinement is bounded
and preserves the original; live disagreement only vetoes with proven FOV/exposure
alignment, which the current capture path does not claim.

Before a production engine switch: collect/split/annotate the real corpus, freeze
resource budgets and configs, run the common evaluator and paired clip/session
statistics, and apply the unchanged §22 rule. Neither reference parity nor a
synthetic fixture percentage substitutes for those steps. Final qualification,
thermal/energy, PSS and physical overlay alignment remain open.

FILE: docs/document-boundary-quality/runs/boundary-review-0.4.286/Main.kt

package app.docscan.android

import org.opencv.core.CvType
import org.opencv.core.Mat
import org.opencv.core.Point
import kotlin.math.hypot
import kotlin.math.roundToInt

private data class CaseData(val name:String,val gray:ByteArray,val edges:ByteArray,val paper:ByteArray,val rgb:ByteArray?,val quad:List<Point>)
private const val W=200
private const val H=200
private val A=intArrayOf(40,40,150)
private val B=intArrayOf(40,60,50)
private val QUAD=listOf(Point(60.0,60.0),Point(140.0,60.0),Point(140.0,140.0),Point(60.0,140.0))
private fun base(name:String,colorMode:String="step",edgeMode:String="all",luma:Boolean=false,hasColor:Boolean=true):CaseData {
    val gray=ByteArray(W*H); val paper=ByteArray(W*H); val edges=ByteArray(W*H); val rgb=ByteArray(W*H*3)
    for(y in 0 until H) for(x in 0 until W) {
        val i=y*W+x; val inside=x in 60..140 && y in 60..140
        if(inside) paper[i]=255.toByte()
        val color=when(colorMode) {
            "uniform" -> B
            "isolated" -> if(inside && y in 60..62 && x in 94..106) A else B
            else -> if(inside) A else B
        }
        gray[i]=(if(luma) if(inside) 90 else 40 else 53).toByte()
        for(c in 0..2) rgb[i*3+c]=color[c].toByte()
    }
    if(edgeMode!="none") for(p in 60..140) {
        if(edgeMode!="missing-left") edges[60*W+p]=255.toByte()
        edges[140*W+p]=255.toByte(); edges[p*W+140]=255.toByte()
        if(edgeMode!="missing-left") edges[p*W+60]=255.toByte()
    }
    return CaseData(name,gray,edges,paper,if(hasColor) rgb else null,QUAD)
}
private fun alternating():CaseData {
    val c=base("alternating near/far direction blocks",colorMode="uniform")
    val rgb=c.rgb!!
    for(side in 0..3) {
        val a=QUAD[side]; val b=QUAD[(side+1)%4]; val dx=b.x-a.x; val dy=b.y-a.y; val len=hypot(dx,dy)
        var nx=-dy/len; var ny=dx/len
        if(nx*(100.0-(a.x+b.x)/2)+ny*(100.0-(a.y+b.y)/2)<0) { nx=-nx; ny=-ny }
        for(i in 0 until 40) {
            val t=.05+.90*i/39; val x=a.x+dx*t; val y=a.y+dy*t
            val forward=i<20
            val inside=if(forward) A else B; val outside=if(forward) B else A
            for(d in listOf(2.0,12.0,20.0)) {
                val ix=(x+nx*d).roundToInt(); val iy=(y+ny*d).roundToInt(); val ox=(x-nx*d).roundToInt(); val oy=(y-ny*d).roundToInt()
                val ii=(iy*W+ix)*3; val oi=(oy*W+ox)*3
                for(ch in 0..2) { rgb[ii+ch]=inside[ch].toByte(); rgb[oi+ch]=outside[ch].toByte() }
            }
        }
    }
    return c.copy(rgb=rgb)
}
private fun randomTexture():CaseData {
    val root=java.io.File("/tmp/docscan-sampler-probe")
    return CaseData("real cv2 random constant-Y chroma texture",java.io.File(root,"random-gray.bin").readBytes(),
        java.io.File(root,"random-edges.bin").readBytes(),java.io.File(root,"random-mask.bin").readBytes(),
        java.io.File(root,"random-rgb.bin").readBytes(),QUAD)
}
private fun evaluate(c:CaseData) {
    val g=Mat(W,H,1,c.gray,CvType.CV_8UC1); val e=Mat(W,H,1,c.edges,CvType.CV_8UC1); val p=Mat(W,H,1,c.paper,CvType.CV_8UC1)
    val color=c.rgb?.let { Mat(W,H,3,it,CvType.CV_8UC3) }
    val assessment=DocumentBoundaryEvidenceSampler(g,e,p,color).assess(c.quad)
    println("${c.name}: coverage=${assessment.sides.map{it.coverage}}, colorSamples=${assessment.sides.map{it.colorSupportedSamples}}, colorBins=${assessment.sides.map{it.colorOccupiedBins}}, luma=${assessment.sides.map{it.availableContextContrast}}, chroma=${assessment.sides.map{it.chromaticTransition}}, fourSides=${assessment.hasFourObservedSides}")
}
fun main() {
    evaluate(base("same-gray material boundary"))
    evaluate(base("uniform",colorMode="uniform"))
    evaluate(base("no edge support",edgeMode="none"))
    evaluate(base("isolated color patch",colorMode="isolated"))
    evaluate(alternating())
    evaluate(base("unsupported one side",edgeMode="missing-left"))
    evaluate(base("strong luminance baseline",luma=true,hasColor=false))
    evaluate(randomTexture())
}

package org.opencv.core

data class Size(val width: Double, val height: Double)
object CvType { const val CV_8UC1=0; const val CV_8U=0; const val CV_8UC3=16 }
class Point(val x: Double, val y: Double)
class Mat(val width: Int, val height: Int, private val channelCount: Int, private val bytes: ByteArray, private val matType: Int) {
    fun cols()=width
    fun rows()=height
    fun channels()=channelCount
    fun type()=matType
    fun depth()=CvType.CV_8U
    fun size()=Size(width.toDouble(),height.toDouble())
    fun get(row: Int,col: Int,dst: ByteArray) { require(row==0 && col==0 && dst.size==bytes.size); bytes.copyInto(dst) }
}

# Boundary color probe — 0.4.286

This folder preserves small host-side reproductions for the color-edge and sampler changes. The production files themselves are referenced, not copied. They were uncommitted working-tree files based on Git `b09f6dc853da639a1d58425849c106cec72df183`; source hashes at probe time are recorded below.

- `Main.kt` compiles and invokes the exact `DocumentBoundaryEvidenceSampler.kt` source against `MatStubs.kt`, minimal byte-array `Mat`/`Point` stand-ins. This checks production Kotlin sampler logic and thresholds without loading OpenCV JNI. It does **not** verify OpenCV `Mat` ABI, native execution, Android, or the full detector.
- `edge_map_probe.py` uses local Python `cv2 5.0.0` to run the same RGB-to-gray/YCrCb conversions, Gaussian blur, Canny thresholds/aperture/L2 mode, and CLAHE grayscale path as `DocumentBoundaryEdgeMap`. It checks edge counts and 40-position side support. This is a host OpenCV mechanism probe, not Android/JNI verification.
- The random constant-Y chromatic texture is generated from 97 RGB values that `cv2.COLOR_RGB2GRAY` maps to 53. Its actual gray/color/edge byte arrays are created under `/tmp/docscan-sampler-probe` and passed to the exact sampler via the stubs; those binary arrays are intentionally not archived here.

Results at probe time:

- Equal-gray material step `(40,40,150)` vs `(40,60,50)`: both RGB colors convert to gray 53; old grayscale edge map has 0 pixels and no supported side samples. Cr/Cb Canny adds 320 edge pixels and yields 40/40 supported positions in 8 bins on each of four sides. The sampler returns true with color support 40/40 per side and zero luma contrast.
- Uniform image has 0 old/chroma/new edges. A small isolated patch does not support all four sides. Missing edge support on one side is rejected. Strong-luma/no-color context remains accepted.
- Random constant-Y chromatic texture: old grayscale map has 0 edges; Cr/Cb map has 24,079 pixels and can support 40/40 positions in all proposed sides. The sampler still returns false: direction-consistent color samples per side are 5, 2, 2, and 3, below 30; luma contrast is zero.
- An alternating-direction synthetic boundary has strong near/far color separation and full edge support, but only 20/40 samples agree in one direction, so the new gate rejects. The prior unsigned rule would count all 40/40 and accept; this is a hand-built sampler profile, not a camera frame.

Production source hashes at probe time:

- `DocumentBoundaryEvidenceSampler.kt`: `1b065526e2248c556571c51250d89083faeaeb0d12e4c555ae8bfeffe7bcbc8e`
- `DocumentBoundaryEdgeMap.kt`: `37ea8776a24846d723dac4710f24bbe8a8d91a22c7cbbae66ec7d40f36a19569`
- `DocumentBoundaryRefiner.kt`: `1fc3f506fae6e51123553eead36da93a88c0afda035dd93f2ab75b3b85a7e966`
- `DocumentBoundaryGradientPeak.kt`: `ce8f8fed3c86c04560869ccb0cbdd2e131b82a5c599a5dc667526fde123392a7`

The two focused Gradle classes passed 17 tests total: 4 `Side`/`Assessment` predicate tests and 13 synthetic 1D peak-profile tests. The latter includes a same-luminance RGB seed where gray strength is zero, the current refiner's seed-channel selection chooses blue, and the signed peak helper keeps the external edge at −0.5 px. This checks the channel-selection arithmetic plus the production peak helper, not `DocumentBoundaryRefiner` with native image access or line fitting. No UI, detector replay, Android, device, or instrumentation tests were run for this probe.

FILE: docs/document-boundary-quality/runs/boundary-review-0.4.286/edge_map_probe.py
