##############################################################################
#
#   Gradle start up script for POSIX generated by Gradle.
#
#   Important for running:
#
#   (1) You need a POSIX-compliant shell to run this script. If your /bin/sh is
#       noncompliant, but you have some other compliant shell such as ksh or
#       bash, then to run this script, type that shell name before the whole
#       command line, like:
#
#           ksh Gradle
#
#       Busybox and similar reduced shells will NOT work, because this script
#       requires all of these POSIX shell features:
#         * functions;
#         * expansions «$var», «${var}», «${var:-default}», «${var+SET}»,
#           «${var#prefix}», «${var%suffix}», and «$( cmd )»;
#         * compound commands having a testable exit status, especially «case»;
#         * various built-in commands including «command», «set», and «ulimit».
#
#   Important for patching:
#
#   (2) This script targets any POSIX shell, so it avoids extensions provided
#       by Bash, Ksh, etc; in particular arrays are avoided.
#
#       The "traditional" practice of packing multiple parameters into a
#       space-separated string is a well documented source of bugs and security
#       problems, so this is (mostly) avoided, by progressively accumulating
#       options in "$@", and eventually passing that to Java.
#
#       Where the inherited environment variables (DEFAULT_JVM_OPTS, JAVA_OPTS,
#       and GRADLE_OPTS) rely on word-splitting, this is performed explicitly;
#       see the in-line comments for details.
#
#       There are tweaks for specific operating systems such as AIX, CygWin,
#       Darwin, MinGW, and NonStop.
#
#   (3) This script is generated from the Groovy template
#       https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/HEAD/platforms/jvm/plugins-application/src/main/resources/org/gradle/api/internal/plugins/unixStartScript.txt
#       within the Gradle project.
#
#       You can find Gradle at https://github.com/gradle/gradle/.
#
##############################################################################

# Attempt to set APP_HOME

# Resolve links: $0 may be a link
app_path=$0

# Need this for daisy-chained symlinks.
while
    APP_HOME=${app_path%"${app_path##*/}"}  # leaves a trailing /; empty if no leading path
    [ -h "$app_path" ]
do
    ls=$( ls -ld "$app_path" )
    link=${ls#*' -> '}
    case $link in             #(
      /*)   app_path=$link ;; #(
      *)    app_path=$APP_HOME$link ;;
    esac
done

# This is normally unused
# shellcheck disable=SC2034
APP_BASE_NAME=${0##*/}
# Discard cd standard output in case $CDPATH is set (https://github.com/gradle/gradle/issues/25036)
APP_HOME=$( cd -P "${APP_HOME:-./}" > /dev/null && printf '%s
' "$PWD" ) || exit

# Use the maximum available, or set MAX_FD != -1 to use that value.
MAX_FD=maximum

warn () {
    echo "$*"
} >&2

die () {
    echo
    echo "$*"
    echo
    exit 1
} >&2

# OS specific support (must be 'true' or 'false').
cygwin=false
msys=false
darwin=false
nonstop=false
case "$( uname )" in                #(
  CYGWIN* )         cygwin=true  ;; #(
  Darwin* )         darwin=true  ;; #(
  MSYS* | MINGW* )  msys=true    ;; #(
  NONSTOP* )        nonstop=true ;;
esac

CLASSPATH=$APP_HOME/gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.jar


# Determine the Java command to use to start the JVM.
if [ -n "$JAVA_HOME" ] ; then
    if [ -x "$JAVA_HOME/jre/sh/java" ] ; then
        # IBM's JDK on AIX uses strange locations for the executables
        JAVACMD=$JAVA_HOME/jre/sh/java
    else
        JAVACMD=$JAVA_HOME/bin/java
    fi
    if [ ! -x "$JAVACMD" ] ; then
        die "ERROR: JAVA_HOME is set to an invalid directory: $JAVA_HOME

Please set the JAVA_HOME variable in your environment to match the
location of your Java installation."
    fi
else
    JAVACMD=java
    if ! command -v java >/dev/null 2>&1
    then
        die "ERROR: JAVA_HOME is not set and no 'java' command could be found in your PATH.

Please set the JAVA_HOME variable in your environment to match the
location of your Java installation."
    fi
fi

# Increase the maximum file descriptors if we can.
if ! "$cygwin" && ! "$darwin" && ! "$nonstop" ; then
    case $MAX_FD in #(
      max*)
        # In POSIX sh, ulimit -H is undefined. That's why the result is checked to see if it worked.
        # shellcheck disable=SC2039,SC3045
        MAX_FD=$( ulimit -H -n ) ||
            warn "Could not query maximum file descriptor limit"
    esac
    case $MAX_FD in  #(
      '' | soft) :;; #(
      *)
        # In POSIX sh, ulimit -n is undefined. That's why the result is checked to see if it worked.
        # shellcheck disable=SC2039,SC3045
        ulimit -n "$MAX_FD" ||
            warn "Could not set maximum file descriptor limit to $MAX_FD"
    esac
fi

# Collect all arguments for the java command, stacking in reverse order:
#   * args from the command line
#   * the main class name
#   * -classpath
#   * -D...appname settings
#   * --module-path (only if needed)
#   * DEFAULT_JVM_OPTS, JAVA_OPTS, and GRADLE_OPTS environment variables.

# For Cygwin or MSYS, switch paths to Windows format before running java
if "$cygwin" || "$msys" ; then
    APP_HOME=$( cygpath --path --mixed "$APP_HOME" )
    CLASSPATH=$( cygpath --path --mixed "$CLASSPATH" )

    JAVACMD=$( cygpath --unix "$JAVACMD" )

    # Now convert the arguments - kludge to limit ourselves to /bin/sh
    for arg do
        if
            case $arg in                                #(
              -*)   false ;;                            # don't mess with options #(
              /?*)  t=${arg#/} t=/${t%%/*}              # looks like a POSIX filepath
                    [ -e "$t" ] ;;                      #(
              *)    false ;;
            esac
        then
            arg=$( cygpath --path --ignore --mixed "$arg" )
        fi
        # Roll the args list around exactly as many times as the number of
        # args, so each arg winds up back in the position where it started, but
        # possibly modified.
        #
        # NB: a `for` loop captures its iteration list before it begins, so
        # changing the positional parameters here affects neither the number of
        # iterations, nor the values presented in `arg`.
        shift                   # remove old arg
        set -- "$@" "$arg"      # push replacement arg
    done
fi


# Add default JVM options here. You can also use JAVA_OPTS and GRADLE_OPTS to pass JVM options to this script.
DEFAULT_JVM_OPTS='"-Xmx64m" "-Xms64m"'

# Collect all arguments for the java command:
#   * DEFAULT_JVM_OPTS, JAVA_OPTS, JAVA_OPTS, and optsEnvironmentVar are not allowed to contain shell fragments,
#     and any embedded shellness will be escaped.
#   * For example: A user cannot expect ${Hostname} to be expanded, as it is an environment variable and will be
#     treated as '${Hostname}' itself on the command line.

set -- \
        "-Dorg.gradle.appname=$APP_BASE_NAME" \
        -classpath "$CLASSPATH" \
        org.gradle.wrapper.GradleWrapperMain \
        "$@"

# Stop when "xargs" is not available.
if ! command -v xargs >/dev/null 2>&1
then
    die "xargs is not available"
fi

# Use "xargs" to parse quoted args.
#
# With -n1 it outputs one arg per line, with the quotes and backslashes removed.
#
# In Bash we could simply go:
#
#   readarray ARGS < <( xargs -n1 <<<"$var" ) &&
#   set -- "${ARGS[@]}" "$@"
#
# but POSIX shell has neither arrays nor command substitution, so instead we
# post-process each arg (as a line of input to sed) to backslash-escape any
# character that might be a shell metacharacter, then use eval to reverse
# that process (while maintaining the separation between arguments), and wrap
# the whole thing up as a single "set" statement.
#
# This will of course break if any of these variables contains a newline or
# an unmatched quote.
#

eval "set -- $(
        printf '%s\n' "$DEFAULT_JVM_OPTS $JAVA_OPTS $GRADLE_OPTS" |
        xargs -n1 |
        sed ' s~[^-[:alnum:]+,./:=@_]~\\&~g; ' |
        tr '\n' ' '
    )" '"$@"'

exec "$JAVACMD" "$@"

@rem This is normally unused

@rem Resolve any "." and ".." in APP_HOME to make it shorter.

@rem Add default JVM options here. You can also use JAVA_OPTS and GRADLE_OPTS to pass JVM options to this script.
set DEFAULT_JVM_OPTS="-Xmx64m" "-Xms64m"

@rem Find java.exe
if defined JAVA_HOME goto findJavaFromJavaHome

set JAVA_EXE=java.exe
%JAVA_EXE% -version >NUL 2>&1
if %ERRORLEVEL% equ 0 goto execute

echo. 1>&2

echo. 1>&2
echo Please set the JAVA_HOME variable in your environment to match the 1>&2
echo location of your Java installation. 1>&2

goto fail

:findJavaFromJavaHome

if exist "%JAVA_EXE%" goto execute

echo. 1>&2
echo ERROR: JAVA_HOME is set to an invalid directory: %JAVA_HOME% 1>&2
echo. 1>&2
echo Please set the JAVA_HOME variable in your environment to match the 1>&2
echo location of your Java installation. 1>&2

goto fail

:execute
@rem Setup the command line

set CLASSPATH=%APP_HOME%\gradle\wrapper\gradle-wrapper.jar


@rem Execute Gradle
"%JAVA_EXE%" %DEFAULT_JVM_OPTS% %JAVA_OPTS% %GRADLE_OPTS% "-Dorg.gradle.appname=%APP_BASE_NAME%" -classpath "%CLASSPATH%" org.gradle.wrapper.GradleWrapperMain %*

:end
@rem End local scope for the variables with windows NT shell

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Summarize files/boundary-telemetry.jsonl from a debug build.

  adb exec-out run-as app.docscan.scanner cat files/boundary-telemetry.jsonl > telemetry.jsonl
  python3 tools/boundary_telemetry_summary.py telemetry.jsonl
"""
import json
import sys
from collections import Counter

live, captures = [], []
for line in open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8"):
    line = line.strip()
    if not line:
        continue
    row = json.loads(line)
    (live if row["type"] == "live" else captures).append(row)

n = sum(r["analyses"] for r in live)
if n:
    found = sum(r["found"] for r in live)
    ui = sum(r["uiEvents"] for r in live) or 1
    shown = sum(r["shown"] for r in live)
    print(f"analyses: {n}; detector found: {found / n:.0%}; overlay shown after hold: {shown / ui:.0%}")
    print(f"avg analysis ms: {sum(r['avgMs'] * r['analyses'] for r in live) / n:.0f}; max: {max(r['maxMs'] for r in live)}")
    rej = Counter()
    for r in live:
        rej.update(r["rejects"])
    print("candidate rejections:", dict(rej.most_common()))
    # Buckets before 0.4.305 were classical-detector edges (0.2/0.32/0.45/0.7); the "edges" field marks the new ones.
    new = [r for r in live if r.get("edges") == "model-v2"]
    if new:
        nn = sum(r["analyses"] for r in new)
        names = ["no_mask", "<0.1", "0.1-0.3", "0.3-0.5 (hold zone)", "0.5-0.8", ">=0.8"]
        totals = [sum(r["bestScoreBuckets"][i] for r in new) for i in range(6)]
        print("model confidence per analysis:", {k: f"{v / nn:.0%}" for k, v in zip(names, totals)})
        gap = (totals[3]) / nn
        print(f"hold-zone share {gap:.0%}: confidence between the appear (0.5) and hold (0.3) thresholds; "
              "a large share means the frame flickers on weak sheets, a share near 0 means the thresholds are not the limit")
    else:
        names = ["no_candidate", "<0.2", "0.2-0.32", "0.32-0.45", "0.45-0.7", ">=0.7"]
        totals = [sum(r["bestScoreBuckets"][i] for r in live) for i in range(6)]
        print("best score per analysis (classical edges):", {k: f"{v / n:.0%}" for k, v in zip(names, totals)})
    fails = Counter()
    for r in live:
        fails.update(r.get("failures", {}))
    if fails:
        print("analysis failures:", dict(fails.most_common()))
if captures:
    by = Counter((c["outcome"], c["overlayVisible"]) for c in captures)
    print("captures (outcome, frame on screen):", dict(by))
    bad = sum(v for (o, _), v in by.items() if o != "RECTIFY_STILL")
    surprise = sum(v for (o, vis), v in by.items() if o == "RECTIFY_STILL" and not vis)
    print(f"not cropped: {bad / len(captures):.0%}; cropped although no frame was shown: {surprise / len(captures):.0%}")

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Paired, session-clustered comparison of DBQ evaluator reports.

This tool compares only eligible-frame geometric success from dbq_evaluate.py.
It is not an acceptance runner and never chooses a production winner.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import math
import pathlib
import random
import re
import sys
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
from typing import Any


SCHEMA_VERSION = 1
MIN_INDEPENDENT_SESSIONS = 10
NONINFERIORITY_MARGIN = -0.02
SHA256_RE = re.compile(r"^[0-9a-f]{64}$")


class ComparisonError(ValueError):
    """Input does not support a fail-closed paired comparison."""


def _unique_object(pairs: list[tuple[str, Any]]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    out: dict[str, Any] = {}
    for key, value in pairs:
        if key in out:
            raise ComparisonError(f"duplicate JSON object key: {key}")
        out[key] = value
    return out


def read_json(path: str | pathlib.Path) -> Any:
    try:
        return json.loads(pathlib.Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8"), object_pairs_hook=_unique_object,
                          parse_constant=lambda value: (_ for _ in ()).throw(ComparisonError(f"invalid JSON number: {value}")))
    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
        raise ComparisonError(f"cannot read JSON {path}: {exc}") from exc


def sha256_file(path: str | pathlib.Path) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(pathlib.Path(path).read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def canonical_sha256(value: Any) -> str:
    encoded = json.dumps(value, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False).encode("utf-8")
    return hashlib.sha256(encoded).hexdigest()


def _require(condition: bool, message: str) -> None:
    if not condition:
        raise ComparisonError(message)


def _integer(value: Any, label: str) -> int:
    _require(isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool) and value >= 0,
             f"{label} must be a non-negative integer")
    return value


def load_manifest(data: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
    _require(isinstance(data, dict), "cluster manifest must be a JSON object")
    _require(data.get("schemaVersion") == SCHEMA_VERSION, "unsupported manifest schemaVersion")
    gt_hash = data.get("sourceGtSha256")
    _require(isinstance(gt_hash, str) and SHA256_RE.fullmatch(gt_hash) is not None,
             "manifest sourceGtSha256 must be a lowercase SHA-256 hex digest")
    raw_clips = data.get("clips")
    _require(isinstance(raw_clips, dict) and bool(raw_clips), "manifest clips must be a non-empty object")
    clips: dict[str, dict[str, str]] = {}
    for clip_id, identity in raw_clips.items():
        _require(isinstance(clip_id, str) and clip_id.strip(), "clip identity must be a non-empty string")
        _require(isinstance(identity, dict), f"manifest identity for clip {clip_id!r} must be an object")
        session_id, group = identity.get("sessionId"), identity.get("group")
        _require(isinstance(session_id, str) and session_id.strip(), f"missing sessionId for clip {clip_id!r}")
        _require(isinstance(group, str) and group.strip(), f"missing group for clip {clip_id!r}")
        clips[clip_id] = {"sessionId": session_id, "group": group}
    ordinary = data.get("ordinaryGroups", [])
    _require(isinstance(ordinary, list) and all(isinstance(x, str) and x for x in ordinary),
             "ordinaryGroups must be a list of non-empty group names")
    _require(len(set(ordinary)) == len(ordinary), "ordinaryGroups contains duplicates")
    _require(set(ordinary) <= {identity["group"] for identity in clips.values()},
             "ordinaryGroups references a group absent from manifest clips")
    return {"sourceGtSha256": gt_hash, "clips": clips, "ordinaryGroups": ordinary,
            "freeze": data.get("freeze", {})}


def load_report(data: Any, label: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    _require(isinstance(data, dict), f"report {label} must be a JSON object")
    _require(data.get("schemaVersion") == 1, f"report {label} has unsupported schemaVersion")
    hashes = data.get("inputSha256")
    _require(isinstance(hashes, dict), f"report {label} is missing inputSha256")
    gt_hash = hashes.get("gt")
    _require(isinstance(gt_hash, str) and SHA256_RE.fullmatch(gt_hash) is not None,
             f"report {label} inputSha256.gt is missing or invalid")
    frames = data.get("frames")
    _require(isinstance(frames, list), f"report {label} frames must be a list")
    by_key: dict[tuple[str, Any], dict[str, Any]] = {}
    for index, frame in enumerate(frames):
        _require(isinstance(frame, dict), f"report {label} frame {index} must be an object")
        clip_id, frame_id = frame.get("clipId"), frame.get("frameId")
        _require(isinstance(clip_id, str) and clip_id.strip(), f"report {label} frame {index} has invalid clipId")
        _require((isinstance(frame_id, str) and frame_id.strip()) or
                 (isinstance(frame_id, int) and not isinstance(frame_id, bool) and frame_id >= 0),
                 f"report {label} frame {index} has invalid frameId")
        key = (clip_id, frame_id)
        _require(key not in by_key, f"report {label} has duplicate eligible frame key {key!r}")
        success = frame.get("success")
        _require(isinstance(success, bool), f"report {label} frame {key!r} success must be explicit boolean")
        # A failed evaluator row includes both absent predictions and invalid geometry. reason is retained,
        # but success is the evaluator's complete decision bit and is what comparison consumes.
        _require(frame.get("reason") in (None, "missing", "invalid"),
                 f"report {label} frame {key!r} has unexpected reason")
        _require(not success or frame.get("reason") is None,
                 f"report {label} frame {key!r} cannot be successful with a failure reason")
        by_key[key] = {"clipId": clip_id, "frameId": frame_id, "success": success,
                       "reason": frame.get("reason")}
    groups = data.get("groups")
    _require(isinstance(groups, dict), f"report {label} groups must be an object")
    normalized_groups: dict[str, dict[str, int]] = {}
    for group_name, summary in groups.items():
        _require(isinstance(group_name, str) and group_name, f"report {label} has invalid group name")
        _require(isinstance(summary, dict), f"report {label} group {group_name!r} must be an object")
        normalized_groups[group_name] = {name: _integer(summary.get(name), f"report {label} {group_name}.{name}")
                                         for name in ("eligible", "success", "missing", "invalid", "clips")}
    return {"gtHash": gt_hash, "frames": by_key, "groups": normalized_groups}


def _percentile(values: list[float], probability: float) -> float:
    ordered = sorted(values)
    position = (len(ordered) - 1) * probability
    low = math.floor(position)
    high = math.ceil(position)
    if low == high:
        return ordered[low]
    return ordered[low] + (ordered[high] - ordered[low]) * (position - low)


def _metric_counts(rows: list[tuple[str, bool, bool]]) -> dict[str, float | int | None]:
    n = len(rows)
    if not n:
        return {"eligibleFrames": 0, "failureA": 0, "failureB": 0, "failureRateA": None,
                "failureRateB": None, "successRateA": None, "successRateB": None,
                "pairedRelativeFailureReduction": None, "absoluteSuccessDifferenceBMinusA": None}
    fail_a = sum(not a for _, a, _ in rows)
    fail_b = sum(not b for _, _, b in rows)
    success_a = n - fail_a
    success_b = n - fail_b
    return {"eligibleFrames": n, "failureA": fail_a, "failureB": fail_b,
            "failureRateA": fail_a / n, "failureRateB": fail_b / n,
            "successRateA": success_a / n, "successRateB": success_b / n,
            "pairedRelativeFailureReduction": ((fail_a - fail_b) / fail_a) if fail_a else None,
            "absoluteSuccessDifferenceBMinusA": (success_b - success_a) / n}


def compare(report_a: Any, report_b: Any, manifest_data: Any, *, seed: int = 282401,
            repetitions: int = 10000) -> dict[str, Any]:
    _require(isinstance(seed, int) and not isinstance(seed, bool) and seed >= 0, "seed must be non-negative")
    _require(isinstance(repetitions, int) and not isinstance(repetitions, bool) and repetitions >= 100,
             "repetitions must be an integer >= 100")
    manifest = load_manifest(manifest_data)
    a = load_report(report_a, "A")
    b = load_report(report_b, "B")
    _require(a["gtHash"] == manifest["sourceGtSha256"], "report A GT hash does not match cluster manifest")
    _require(b["gtHash"] == manifest["sourceGtSha256"], "report B GT hash does not match cluster manifest")
    keys_a, keys_b = set(a["frames"]), set(b["frames"])
    _require(keys_a == keys_b, f"eligible frame key mismatch: onlyA={len(keys_a-keys_b)} onlyB={len(keys_b-keys_a)}")
    _require(bool(keys_a), "no eligible paired frames")

    frame_groups: dict[str, list[tuple[str, bool, bool]]] = defaultdict(list)
    clip_counts: Counter[str] = Counter()
    expected_clip_frames: Counter[str] = Counter()
    for clip_id, _ in keys_a:
        _require(clip_id in manifest["clips"], f"eligible frame references clip missing from manifest: {clip_id!r}")
        expected_clip_frames[clip_id] += 1
    for key in sorted(keys_a, key=lambda item: (item[0], type(item[1]).__name__, str(item[1]))):
        clip_id, _ = key
        identity = manifest["clips"][clip_id]
        row_a, row_b = a["frames"][key], b["frames"][key]
        _require(row_a["clipId"] == row_b["clipId"] and row_a["frameId"] == row_b["frameId"],
                 f"paired identity mismatch for {key!r}")
        frame_groups[identity["group"]].append((identity["sessionId"], row_a["success"], row_b["success"]))
        clip_counts[identity["group"]] += 0  # group initialized below from unique eligible clips
    for clip_id in expected_clip_frames:
        clip_counts[manifest["clips"][clip_id]["group"]] += 1

    # Reconcile report summaries against the manifest-derived eligible frames and identities.
    manifest_groups = {identity["group"] for identity in manifest["clips"].values()}
    groups = set(frame_groups) | set(a["groups"]) | set(b["groups"]) | manifest_groups
    for label, report in (("A", a), ("B", b)):
        for group_name in groups:
            summary = report["groups"].get(group_name)
            expected_n = len(frame_groups.get(group_name, []))
            expected_success = sum(row[1 if label == "A" else 2] for row in frame_groups.get(group_name, []))
            expected_clips = clip_counts.get(group_name, 0)
            eligible_clip_ids = {clip_id for clip_id, _ in keys_a
                                 if manifest["clips"][clip_id]["group"] == group_name}
            expected_missing = sum(report["frames"][key]["reason"] == "missing" for key in keys_a
                                   if key[0] in eligible_clip_ids)
            expected_invalid = sum(report["frames"][key]["reason"] == "invalid" for key in keys_a
                                   if key[0] in eligible_clip_ids)
            _require(summary is not None, f"report {label} missing group summary {group_name!r}")
            _require(summary["eligible"] == expected_n, f"report {label} {group_name}.eligible disagrees with frames/manifest")
            _require(summary["success"] == expected_success, f"report {label} {group_name}.success disagrees with frames")
            _require(summary["clips"] == expected_clips, f"report {label} {group_name}.clips disagrees with manifest")
            _require(summary["missing"] == expected_missing, f"report {label} {group_name}.missing disagrees with frames")
            _require(summary["invalid"] == expected_invalid, f"report {label} {group_name}.invalid disagrees with frames")
            _require(summary["missing"] + summary["invalid"] <= summary["eligible"] - summary["success"],
                     f"report {label} {group_name} failure counters exceed failures")

    sessions = sorted({session_id for rows in frame_groups.values() for session_id, _, _ in rows})
    _require(bool(sessions), "no independent session clusters")
    point: dict[str, Any] = {}
    bootstrap_values: dict[str, dict[str, list[float]]] = {}
    for group_name in sorted(groups):
        rows = frame_groups.get(group_name, [])
        values = _metric_counts(rows)
        session_ids = {session_id for session_id, _, _ in rows}
        values["independentSessions"] = len(session_ids)
        values["independentClips"] = clip_counts[group_name]
        values["pairedRelativeFailureReductionCI95TwoSided"] = None
        values["absoluteSuccessDifferenceCI95TwoSided"] = None
        values["nonInferiorityLowerBound95OneSided"] = None
        values["nonInferiorityMargin"] = NONINFERIORITY_MARGIN if group_name in manifest["ordinaryGroups"] else None
        values["nonInferiorityStatus"] = "NOT_APPLICABLE" if group_name not in manifest["ordinaryGroups"] else "INCONCLUSIVE"
        values["absoluteIntervalStatus"] = "INCONCLUSIVE"
        values["relativeIntervalStatus"] = "UNAVAILABLE" if values["pairedRelativeFailureReduction"] is None else "INCONCLUSIVE"
        point[group_name] = values
        bootstrap_values[group_name] = {"relative": [], "absolute": []}

    rows_by_session: dict[str, dict[str, list[tuple[str, bool, bool]]]] = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(list))
    for group_name, rows in frame_groups.items():
        for row in rows:
            rows_by_session[row[0]][group_name].append(row)
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    invalid_replicates: Counter[str] = Counter()
    degenerate_groups: set[str] = set()
    all_bootstrap: dict[str, dict[str, list[float]]] = {name: {"relative": [], "absolute": []} for name in frame_groups}
    for group_name in sorted(groups):
        rows = frame_groups.get(group_name, [])
        group_sessions = sorted({session_id for session_id, _, _ in rows})
        if not group_sessions:
            invalid_replicates[group_name] = repetitions
            continue
        for _ in range(repetitions):
            # Resample only independent sessions represented in this group. Within every selected
            # session, include all its group clips and frames together.
            sampled_sessions = [group_sessions[rng.randrange(len(group_sessions))] for _ in group_sessions]
            sample_rows: list[tuple[str, bool, bool]] = []
            for session_id in sampled_sessions:
                sample_rows.extend(rows_by_session[session_id][group_name])
            sample_metrics = _metric_counts(sample_rows)
            relative = sample_metrics["pairedRelativeFailureReduction"]
            absolute = sample_metrics["absoluteSuccessDifferenceBMinusA"]
            if relative is None:
                invalid_replicates[group_name] += 1
            else:
                all_bootstrap[group_name]["relative"].append(float(relative))
            all_bootstrap[group_name]["absolute"].append(float(absolute))

    for group_name, values in point.items():
        group_sessions = values["independentSessions"]
        relative_samples = all_bootstrap[group_name]["relative"]
        absolute_samples = all_bootstrap[group_name]["absolute"]
        no_frames_in_draws = len(absolute_samples) != repetitions
        zero_a_failure_count = invalid_replicates[group_name]
        zero_a_failure_draws = zero_a_failure_count > 0
        flat_absolute = len(set(absolute_samples)) <= 1
        flat_relative = values["pairedRelativeFailureReduction"] is not None and len(set(relative_samples)) <= 1
        tiny = group_sessions < MIN_INDEPENDENT_SESSIONS
        if tiny:
            degenerate_groups.add(group_name)
        reasons = []
        if tiny:
            reasons.append(f"only {group_sessions} independent sessions; minimum is {MIN_INDEPENDENT_SESSIONS}")
        if values["eligibleFrames"] == 0:
            reasons.append("no eligible paired frames in this group")
        if no_frames_in_draws:
            reasons.append("some bootstrap samples had no group frames")
        if flat_absolute:
            reasons.append("absolute-effect bootstrap distribution is degenerate; flat bootstrap does not establish zero risk")
        if tiny or no_frames_in_draws or flat_absolute:
            values["absoluteIntervalStatus"] = "INCONCLUSIVE"
        else:
            values["absoluteIntervalStatus"] = "ESTIMATED"
        if values["pairedRelativeFailureReduction"] is None:
            values["relativeIntervalStatus"] = "UNAVAILABLE"
            reasons.append("relative failure reduction is unavailable because A has zero observed failures")
        elif tiny or zero_a_failure_draws or flat_relative:
            values["relativeIntervalStatus"] = "INCONCLUSIVE"
            if zero_a_failure_draws:
                reasons.append(f"{zero_a_failure_count} bootstrap samples had zero A failures")
            if flat_relative:
                reasons.append("relative-effect bootstrap distribution is degenerate; flat bootstrap does not establish zero risk")
        else:
            values["relativeIntervalStatus"] = "ESTIMATED"
        values["intervalStatus"] = ("ESTIMATED" if values["absoluteIntervalStatus"] == "ESTIMATED"
                                     and values["relativeIntervalStatus"] == "ESTIMATED" else "INCONCLUSIVE")
        values["intervalReasons"] = reasons
        if len(absolute_samples) == repetitions:
            values["absoluteSuccessDifferenceCI95TwoSided"] = [_percentile(absolute_samples, .025),
                                                                  _percentile(absolute_samples, .975)]
            values["nonInferiorityLowerBound95OneSided"] = _percentile(absolute_samples, .05)
        if values["pairedRelativeFailureReduction"] is not None and len(relative_samples) == repetitions:
            values["pairedRelativeFailureReductionCI95TwoSided"] = [_percentile(relative_samples, .025),
                                                                      _percentile(relative_samples, .975)]
        if group_name in manifest["ordinaryGroups"]:
            lower = values["nonInferiorityLowerBound95OneSided"]
            if values["absoluteIntervalStatus"] == "ESTIMATED" and lower is not None:
                values["nonInferiorityStatus"] = "PASS" if lower >= NONINFERIORITY_MARGIN else "FAIL"
            else:
                values["nonInferiorityStatus"] = "INCONCLUSIVE"

    freeze = manifest["freeze"]
    freeze_reasons = []
    if not isinstance(freeze, dict):
        freeze_reasons.append("manifest freeze metadata is absent or malformed")
    else:
        if freeze.get("independentCorpusFrozen") is not True:
            freeze_reasons.append("independent corpus freeze is not attested")
        if not isinstance(freeze.get("ciPlan"), dict) or not freeze["ciPlan"]:
            freeze_reasons.append("predeclared CI plan is absent")
        if not isinstance(freeze.get("hardwareGates"), dict) or not freeze["hardwareGates"]:
            freeze_reasons.append("hardware gates are absent")
        if not isinstance(freeze.get("resourceGates"), dict) or not freeze["resourceGates"]:
            freeze_reasons.append("resource gates are absent")
    selection_reasons = freeze_reasons + [
        "this paired geometry harness does not evaluate all absolute AC, hardware, or resource gates",
        "winner selection requires a separate evidence-backed decision record"
    ]
    return {
        "schemaVersion": SCHEMA_VERSION,
        "scope": "paired eligible-frame geometry comparison; original-pixel replay only",
        "selection": {"status": "INCONCLUSIVE", "winner": None, "reasons": selection_reasons},
        "protocol": {
            "independentUnit": "sessionId cluster; every clip and eligible frame in a sampled session is resampled jointly",
            "bootstrap": "ordinary percentile cluster bootstrap with replacement",
            "seed": seed,
            "repetitions": repetitions,
            "intervals": {"effect": "two-sided 95% percentile CI (2.5%, 97.5%)",
                          "ordinaryGroupNonInferiority": "one-sided 95% lower percentile bound (5%)"},
            "pointWeighting": "frame-weighted within each group; groups reported separately",
            "nonInferiorityMargin": NONINFERIORITY_MARGIN,
            "minimumIndependentSessionsPerGroup": MIN_INDEPENDENT_SESSIONS,
            "zeroAFailureRelativeReduction": "unavailable; never treated as infinite or zero",
        },
        "inputs": {"reportASha256": None, "reportBSha256": None, "manifestSha256": None,
                   "sourceGtSha256": manifest["sourceGtSha256"], "clusterManifestSha256": None,
                   "clusterAssignmentsSha256": canonical_sha256(manifest["clips"])},
        "counts": {"pairedEligibleFrames": len(keys_a), "groups": len(frame_groups),
                   "independentSessions": len(sessions), "bootstrapDegenerateGroups": sorted(degenerate_groups)},
        "groups": point,
    }


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--report-a", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--report-b", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--manifest", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--output", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=282401)
    parser.add_argument("--repetitions", type=int, default=10000)
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    try:
        report_a = read_json(args.report_a)
        report_b = read_json(args.report_b)
        manifest = read_json(args.manifest)
        result = compare(report_a, report_b, manifest, seed=args.seed, repetitions=args.repetitions)
        result["inputs"].update({"reportASha256": sha256_file(args.report_a),
                                 "reportBSha256": sha256_file(args.report_b),
                                 "manifestSha256": sha256_file(args.manifest),
                                 "clusterManifestSha256": sha256_file(args.manifest)})
        pathlib.Path(args.output).write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2, allow_nan=False) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
        print(json.dumps({"output": args.output, "selection": result["selection"], "counts": result["counts"]},
                         sort_keys=True))
        return 0
    except (ComparisonError, OSError, TypeError) as exc:
        print(f"dbq_compare: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())


================================================================================
FILE: tools/dbq_evaluate.py
================================================================================

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""DBQ geometric replay evaluator. No physical/UI/latency or acceptance claims.
JSONL GT: clipId, frameId, group, eligible, quad (4 [x,y] in original pixels).
JSONL predictions: clipId, frameId, quad (or null). Missing predictions are failures.
"""
import argparse, json, math, pathlib, hashlib


def cross(a,b,c):
    return (b[0]-a[0])*(c[1]-b[1])-(b[1]-a[1])*(c[0]-b[0])


def validate(q):
    if not isinstance(q,list) or len(q)!=4: raise ValueError('expected four ordered points')
    if any(not isinstance(p,list) or len(p)!=2 or any(not isinstance(v,(float,int)) or isinstance(v,bool) or not math.isfinite(v) for v in p) for p in q):
        raise ValueError('non-finite or malformed points')
    turns=[cross(q[i],q[(i+1)%4],q[(i+2)%4]) for i in range(4)]
    if not(all(t>1e-9 for t in turns) or all(t < -1e-9 for t in turns)):
        raise ValueError('non-convex, degenerate or self-intersecting quad')
    return q


def signed_area(p):
    return sum(a[0]*b[1]-b[0]*a[1] for a,b in zip(p,p[1:]+p[:1]))/2 if len(p)>2 else 0


def intersection(subject,clip):
    output=subject[:]
    orientation=1 if signed_area(clip)>0 else -1
    for a,b in zip(clip,clip[1:]+clip[:1]):
        old=output; output=[]
        if not old: break
        def distance(p): return orientation*((b[0]-a[0])*(p[1]-a[1])-(b[1]-a[1])*(p[0]-a[0]))
        previous=old[-1]; dp=distance(previous)
        for point in old:
            dc=distance(point)
            if (dc>=0)!=(dp>=0):
                t=dp/(dp-dc)
                output.append([previous[0]+t*(point[0]-previous[0]),previous[1]+t*(point[1]-previous[1])])
            if dc>=0: output.append(point)
            previous=point; dp=dc
    return output


def geometry(predicted,ground_truth):
    p=validate(predicted); g=validate(ground_truth)
    ai=abs(signed_area(intersection(p,g))); union=abs(signed_area(p))+abs(signed_area(g))-ai
    if union<=0: raise ValueError('zero union')
    diagonal=max(math.dist(g[0],g[2]),math.dist(g[1],g[3]))
    # Reverse winding to match GT; validate() already rejects crossed vertices.
    if signed_area(p)*signed_area(g)<0: p=list(reversed(p))
    errors=[max(math.dist(p[(i+shift)%4],g[i]) for i in range(4)) for shift in range(4)]
    error=min(errors)/diagonal
    shift=errors.index(min(errors)); aligned=[p[(i+shift)%4] for i in range(4)]
    # Mean absolute normal distance of corresponding side endpoints, divided by GT short side.
    short=min(math.dist(g[i],g[(i+1)%4]) for i in range(4))
    side=[]
    for i in range(4):
        a=g[i]; b=g[(i+1)%4]; length=math.dist(a,b)
        side.append(sum(abs((b[0]-a[0])*(v[1]-a[1])-(b[1]-a[1])*(v[0]-a[0]))/length for v in (aligned[i],aligned[(i+1)%4]))/2/short)
    return {'iou':ai/union,'cornerError':error,'maxSideError':max(side)}


def load(path):
    values={}
    for line in pathlib.Path(path).read_text().splitlines():
        if not line.strip(): continue
        row=json.loads(line); key=(row['clipId'],row['frameId'])
        if key in values: raise ValueError('duplicate frame key: '+str(key))
        values[key]=row
    return values


def evaluate(gt,predictions):
    groups={}; frames=[]
    for key,row in gt.items():
        if not isinstance(row.get('eligible'),bool): raise ValueError('GT eligibility must be explicit')
        group=groups.setdefault(row['group'],{'eligible':0,'success':0,'missing':0,'invalid':0,'excluded':0,'clips':set()})
        if not row['eligible']: group['excluded']+=1; continue
        validate(row['quad']); group['eligible']+=1; group['clips'].add(row['clipId'])
        predicted=predictions.get(key,{}).get('quad')
        reason=None; metric=None
        if predicted is None: reason='missing'; group['missing']+=1
        else:
            try: metric=geometry(predicted,row['quad'])
            except ValueError: reason='invalid'; group['invalid']+=1
        success=metric is not None and metric['iou']>=0.97 and metric['cornerError']<=0.01
        group['success']+=int(success)
        frames.append({'clipId':key[0],'frameId':key[1],'success':success,'reason':reason,'geometry':metric})
    for group in groups.values():
        group['clips']=len(group['clips'])
        group['successRate']=group['success']/group['eligible'] if group['eligible'] else None
        group['acceptance']='INCONCLUSIVE' # no frozen independent corpus / CI / physical evidence
    return {'schemaVersion':1,'scope':'original-pixel geometry replay only','groups':groups,'frames':frames,
        'extraPredictions':len(set(predictions)-set(gt)),
        'physicalAcceptance':'NOT_RUN','confirmedPrecision':None,'displayedJitter':None,'captureToPresent':None}


def main():
    parser=argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument('--gt',required=True); parser.add_argument('--predictions',required=True); parser.add_argument('--output',required=True)
    args=parser.parse_args(); result=evaluate(load(args.gt),load(args.predictions))
    result['inputSha256']={name:hashlib.sha256(pathlib.Path(path).read_bytes()).hexdigest() for name,path in [('gt',args.gt),('predictions',args.predictions)]}
    pathlib.Path(args.output).write_text(json.dumps(result,indent=2,allow_nan=False)+'\n')

if __name__=='__main__': main()


================================================================================
FILE: tools/dbq_replay_to_evaluator.py
================================================================================

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Convert one completed AndroidTest DBQ replay run into evaluator JSONL inputs."""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import math
import pathlib
import re
import sys
from typing import Any

import dbq_evaluate


ID_RE = re.compile(r"^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,80}$")
SHA_RE = re.compile(r"^[0-9a-f]{64}$")
SAFE_OUTPUT_RE = re.compile(r"^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$")


class ReplayConversionError(ValueError):
    """Replay output is incomplete or inconsistent with its source manifest."""


def _unique_object(pairs: list[tuple[str, Any]]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    result: dict[str, Any] = {}
    for key, value in pairs:
        if key in result:
            raise ReplayConversionError(f"duplicate JSON object key: {key}")
        result[key] = value
    return result


def _bad_constant(value: str) -> None:
    raise ReplayConversionError(f"invalid JSON number: {value}")


def _load_json(path: pathlib.Path) -> Any:
    try:
        return json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), object_pairs_hook=_unique_object,
                          parse_constant=_bad_constant)
    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
        raise ReplayConversionError(f"cannot read JSON {path}: {exc}") from exc


def _sha256_bytes(data: bytes) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()


def _require(condition: bool, message: str) -> None:
    if not condition:
        raise ReplayConversionError(message)


def _safe_id(value: Any, label: str) -> str:
    _require(isinstance(value, str) and ID_RE.fullmatch(value) is not None and value not in (".", ".."),
             f"{label} must use 1-80 ASCII letters, digits, dot, underscore, or dash")
    return value


def _frame_id(value: Any, label: str) -> int:
    _require(isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool) and value >= 0,
             f"{label} must be the non-negative integer used by replay schema v1")
    return value


def _finite_number(value: Any) -> bool:
    if not isinstance(value, (int, float)) or isinstance(value, bool):
        return False
    try:
        return math.isfinite(float(value))
    except (OverflowError, ValueError):
        return False


def _sha(value: Any, label: str) -> str:
    _require(isinstance(value, str) and SHA_RE.fullmatch(value) is not None,
             f"{label} must be a lowercase SHA-256 hex digest")
    return value


def _point_list(value: Any, label: str, *, required: bool) -> list[list[float | int]] | None:
    if value is None:
        _require(not required, f"{label} is required for eligible ground truth")
        return None
    _require(isinstance(value, list) and len(value) == 4, f"{label} must be null or four [x,y] points")
    points: list[list[float | int]] = []
    for index, point in enumerate(value):
        _require(isinstance(point, list) and len(point) == 2, f"{label}[{index}] must be [x,y]")
        for coordinate in point:
            _require(_finite_number(coordinate), f"{label}[{index}] has a non-finite or invalid coordinate")
        points.append([point[0], point[1]])
    return points


def _manifest_quad(value: Any, *, eligible: bool, label: str) -> list[list[float | int]] | None:
    if value is None:
        _require(not eligible, f"{label} is null for eligible frame")
        return None
    _require(isinstance(value, list) and len(value) == 8, f"{label} must be null or eight flat coordinates")
    _require(all(_finite_number(v) for v in value),
             f"{label} has non-finite or invalid coordinates")
    nested = [[value[i], value[i + 1]] for i in range(0, 8, 2)]
    try:
        metrics = dbq_evaluate.geometry(nested, nested)
        _require(all(math.isfinite(metric) for metric in metrics.values()), f"{label} has non-finite geometry")
    except (ValueError, OverflowError) as exc:
        raise ReplayConversionError(f"{label} is invalid ground truth: {exc}") from exc
    return nested


def _read_manifest(path: pathlib.Path) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], dict[tuple[str, int], dict[str, Any]], list[str], list[str], str]:
    _require(path.is_file(), f"real source manifest is missing: {path}")
    manifest_bytes = path.read_bytes()
    manifest_sha = _sha256_bytes(manifest_bytes)
    manifest = _load_json(path)
    _require(isinstance(manifest, dict) and manifest.get("schemaVersion") == 1,
             "source manifest must be an object with schemaVersion 1")
    variants_raw, clips_raw = manifest.get("variants"), manifest.get("clips")
    _require(isinstance(variants_raw, list) and bool(variants_raw), "source manifest variants must be a non-empty list")
    _require(isinstance(clips_raw, list) and bool(clips_raw), "source manifest clips must be a non-empty list")
    variant_ids: list[str] = []
    for row in variants_raw:
        _require(isinstance(row, dict), "source manifest variant must be an object")
        variant_id = _safe_id(row.get("id"), "variant id")
        _require(variant_id not in variant_ids, f"duplicate variant id: {variant_id}")
        variant_ids.append(variant_id)
    clips: list[str] = []
    frames: dict[tuple[str, int], dict[str, Any]] = {}
    for clip in clips_raw:
        _require(isinstance(clip, dict), "source manifest clip must be an object")
        clip_id = _safe_id(clip.get("clipId"), "clipId")
        group = clip.get("group")
        _require(isinstance(group, str) and group.strip(), f"clip {clip_id!r} has invalid group")
        _require(clip_id not in clips, f"duplicate clipId in source manifest: {clip_id}")
        clips.append(clip_id)
        frame_rows = clip.get("frames")
        _require(isinstance(frame_rows, list) and bool(frame_rows), f"clip {clip_id!r} frames must be non-empty")
        for frame in frame_rows:
            _require(isinstance(frame, dict), f"clip {clip_id!r} frame must be an object")
            frame_id = _frame_id(frame.get("frameId"), f"clip {clip_id!r} frameId")
            key = (clip_id, frame_id)
            _require(key not in frames, f"duplicate source manifest frame identity: {key!r}")
            eligible = frame.get("eligible")
            _require(isinstance(eligible, bool), f"source manifest frame {key!r} eligible must be boolean")
            quad = _manifest_quad(frame.get("quad"), eligible=eligible, label=f"source manifest frame {key!r} quad")
            frames[key] = {"clipId": clip_id, "frameId": frame_id, "group": group,
                           "eligible": eligible, "quad": quad}
    return manifest, frames, variant_ids, clips, manifest_sha


def _read_jsonl(path: pathlib.Path) -> tuple[list[dict[str, Any]], str]:
    _require(path.is_file() and not path.is_symlink(), f"missing or unsafe replay JSONL file: {path.name}")
    content = path.read_bytes()
    try:
        lines = content.decode("utf-8").splitlines()
    except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
        raise ReplayConversionError(f"replay JSONL is not UTF-8: {path.name}") from exc
    rows: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    for line_number, line in enumerate(lines, 1):
        if not line.strip():
            continue
        try:
            row = json.loads(line, object_pairs_hook=_unique_object, parse_constant=_bad_constant)
        except (json.JSONDecodeError, ReplayConversionError) as exc:
            raise ReplayConversionError(f"invalid JSONL {path.name}:{line_number}: {exc}") from exc
        _require(isinstance(row, dict), f"JSONL {path.name}:{line_number} must contain an object")
        rows.append(row)
    return rows, _sha256_bytes(content)


def convert_run(input_dir: str | pathlib.Path, manifest_path: str | pathlib.Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Validate a completed replay run and return canonical evaluator input bytes + provenance."""
    source_dir = pathlib.Path(input_dir)
    _require(source_dir.is_dir(), f"input replay run directory does not exist: {source_dir}")
    run_path = source_dir / "run.json"
    _require(run_path.is_file(), "replay run metadata run.json is required")
    run = _load_json(run_path)
    _require(isinstance(run, dict) and run.get("schemaVersion") == 1, "run.json must use schemaVersion 1")
    _require(run.get("status") == "COMPLETED", "replay run status must be COMPLETED; NOT_RUN is not a passing input")
    manifest, gt_frames, variant_ids, clip_ids, manifest_sha = _read_manifest(pathlib.Path(manifest_path))
    run_manifest_sha = _sha(run.get("sourceManifestSha256"), "run.json sourceManifestSha256")
    _require(run_manifest_sha == manifest_sha, "source manifest SHA does not match run.json")
    run_variants = run.get("variants")
    _require(isinstance(run_variants, list), "run.json variants must be a list")
    run_variant_ids = []
    for row in run_variants:
        _require(isinstance(row, dict), "run.json variant entry must be an object")
        run_variant_ids.append(_safe_id(row.get("variantId"), "run.json variantId"))
    _require(run_variant_ids == variant_ids, "run.json variant identities/order disagree with source manifest")
    run_clips = run.get("clipIds")
    _require(run_clips == clip_ids, "run.json clipIds/order disagree with source manifest")
    run_row_count = run.get("rowCount")
    _require(isinstance(run_row_count, int) and not isinstance(run_row_count, bool) and run_row_count >= 0,
             "run.json rowCount must be a non-negative integer")

    expected_names = {f"{variant_id}--{clip_id}.jsonl" for variant_id in variant_ids for clip_id in clip_ids}
    actual_paths = [p for p in source_dir.iterdir() if p.name.endswith(".jsonl")]
    actual_names = {p.name for p in actual_paths}
    _require(actual_names == expected_names,
             f"replay JSONL file set mismatch: missing={sorted(expected_names-actual_names)} extra={sorted(actual_names-expected_names)}")

    rows_by_variant: dict[str, dict[tuple[str, int], dict[str, Any]]] = {v: {} for v in variant_ids}
    jsonl_hashes: dict[str, str] = {}
    total_rows = 0
    expected_keys = set(gt_frames)
    for variant_id in variant_ids:
        for clip_id in clip_ids:
            name = f"{variant_id}--{clip_id}.jsonl"
            path = source_dir / name
            _require(not path.is_symlink(), f"replay JSONL must not be a symlink: {name}")
            rows, digest = _read_jsonl(path)
            jsonl_hashes[name] = digest
            for row in rows:
                total_rows += 1
                required_fields = {"schemaVersion", "sourceManifestSha256", "variantId", "clipId", "group",
                                   "frameId", "inputSha256", "eligible", "referenceQuadPixelCentres",
                                   "publishedQuadPixelCentres"}
                _require(required_fields <= set(row),
                         f"{name} row is missing required fields: {sorted(required_fields-set(row))}")
                _require(row.get("schemaVersion") == 1, f"{name} row has unsupported schemaVersion")
                row_variant = _safe_id(row.get("variantId"), f"{name} variantId")
                row_clip = _safe_id(row.get("clipId"), f"{name} clipId")
                row_frame = _frame_id(row.get("frameId"), f"{name} frameId")
                _require(row_variant == variant_id and row_clip == clip_id,
                         f"row identity does not match JSONL filename {name}")
                key = (row_clip, row_frame)
                _require(key in gt_frames, f"row references frame absent from source manifest: {key!r}")
                _require(key not in rows_by_variant[variant_id], f"duplicate replay frame identity for {variant_id}: {key!r}")
                source_sha = _sha(row.get("sourceManifestSha256"), f"{name} sourceManifestSha256")
                _require(source_sha == manifest_sha, f"{name} sourceManifestSha256 mismatch")
                expected = gt_frames[key]
                _require(row.get("group") == expected["group"], f"group label mismatch for {variant_id} {key!r}")
                _require(row.get("eligible") is expected["eligible"], f"eligibility label mismatch for {variant_id} {key!r}")
                reference = _point_list(row.get("referenceQuadPixelCentres"), f"{name} {key!r} referenceQuadPixelCentres",
                                        required=expected["eligible"])
                _require(reference == expected["quad"], f"ground-truth quad mismatch for {variant_id} {key!r}")
                input_sha = _sha(row.get("inputSha256"), f"{name} {key!r} inputSha256")
                published = _point_list(row.get("publishedQuadPixelCentres"),
                                        f"{name} {key!r} publishedQuadPixelCentres", required=False)
                if expected["eligible"] and published is not None:
                    try:
                        metrics = dbq_evaluate.geometry(published, expected["quad"])
                    except ValueError:
                        # Preserve invalid but structurally valid published geometry so the evaluator
                        # records it as an invalid-frame failure.
                        pass
                    except OverflowError as exc:
                        raise ReplayConversionError(f"published geometry overflows evaluator arithmetic for {key!r}") from exc
                    else:
                        _require(all(math.isfinite(metric) for metric in metrics.values()),
                                 f"published geometry has non-finite evaluator metrics for {key!r}")
                rows_by_variant[variant_id][key] = {"inputSha256": input_sha,
                                                     "publishedQuadPixelCentres": published}
            expected_clip_keys = {key for key in expected_keys if key[0] == clip_id}
            _require(expected_clip_keys <= set(rows_by_variant[variant_id]),
                     f"missing replay frame keys for {variant_id}/{clip_id}")
    _require(total_rows == run_row_count, "JSONL row count does not match run.json rowCount")
    for variant_id in variant_ids:
        _require(set(rows_by_variant[variant_id]) == expected_keys,
                 f"replay frame key set does not match manifest for variant {variant_id}")
    for key in sorted(expected_keys, key=lambda item: (item[0], type(item[1]).__name__, str(item[1]))):
        hashes = {rows_by_variant[v][key]["inputSha256"] for v in variant_ids}
        _require(len(hashes) == 1, f"inputSha256 differs across variants for frame {key!r}")

    ordered_frames = [gt_frames[key] for clip_id in clip_ids for key in gt_frames if key[0] == clip_id]
    gt_lines = [json.dumps({"clipId": frame["clipId"], "frameId": frame["frameId"],
                            "group": frame["group"], "eligible": frame["eligible"], "quad": frame["quad"]},
                           separators=(",", ":"), allow_nan=False) for frame in ordered_frames]
    outputs: dict[str, bytes] = {"gt.jsonl": ("\n".join(gt_lines) + "\n").encode("utf-8")}
    for variant_id in variant_ids:
        pred_rows = []
        for frame in ordered_frames:
            key = (frame["clipId"], frame["frameId"])
            pred_rows.append(json.dumps({"clipId": frame["clipId"], "frameId": frame["frameId"],
                                         "quad": rows_by_variant[variant_id][key]["publishedQuadPixelCentres"]},
                                        separators=(",", ":"), allow_nan=False))
        outputs[f"predictions-{variant_id}.jsonl"] = ("\n".join(pred_rows) + "\n").encode("utf-8")
    for filename in outputs:
        _require(SAFE_OUTPUT_RE.fullmatch(filename) is not None and pathlib.PurePath(filename).name == filename,
                 f"unsafe output filename derived from replay variant: {filename!r}")
    output_hashes = {name: _sha256_bytes(content) for name, content in outputs.items()}
    provenance = {
        "schemaVersion": 1,
        "status": "CONVERTED",
        "sourceManifestSha256": manifest_sha,
        "runMetadataSha256": _sha256_bytes(run_path.read_bytes()),
        "sourceManifestPath": str(pathlib.Path(manifest_path).resolve()),
        "replayRunDirectory": str(source_dir.resolve()),
        "replayJsonlSha256": dict(sorted(jsonl_hashes.items())),
        "inputSha256ByFrame": {f"{clip}/{frame}": rows_by_variant[variant_ids[0]][(clip, frame)]["inputSha256"]
                                for clip, frame in sorted(expected_keys, key=lambda item: (item[0], type(item[1]).__name__, str(item[1])))},
        "outputSha256": output_hashes,
        "variants": variant_ids,
        "clipIds": clip_ids,
        "frameCount": len(expected_keys),
        "rowCount": total_rows,
        "claims": {"geometryReplayOnly": True, "latencyOrUiQualityClaim": False,
                   "hardwareAcceptance": "NOT_RUN", "winnerSelection": "NOT_RUN"},
        "clusterManifest": "required separately; no sessionId or corpus independence inferred",
    }
    return {"outputs": outputs, "provenance": provenance}


def convert_to_directory(input_dir: str | pathlib.Path, manifest_path: str | pathlib.Path,
                         output_dir: str | pathlib.Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
    converted = convert_run(input_dir, manifest_path)
    destination = pathlib.Path(output_dir)
    _require(not destination.exists(), f"output directory already exists: {destination}")
    destination.mkdir(parents=True)
    try:
        for name, content in converted["outputs"].items():
            (destination / name).write_bytes(content)
        provenance_bytes = (json.dumps(converted["provenance"], indent=2, allow_nan=False) + "\n").encode("utf-8")
        (destination / "conversion-report.json").write_bytes(provenance_bytes)
    except OSError:
        # A partially written output directory is not a valid conversion artifact.
        for child in destination.iterdir():
            child.unlink()
        destination.rmdir()
        raise
    return converted


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--input-dir", required=True, help="completed replay run directory containing run.json and per-variant JSONL")
    parser.add_argument("--manifest", required=True, help="the exact source replay manifest used for the run")
    parser.add_argument("--output-dir", required=True, help="new directory for canonical evaluator inputs and provenance")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    try:
        converted = convert_to_directory(args.input_dir, args.manifest, args.output_dir)
        print(json.dumps({"status": "CONVERTED", "outputDir": args.output_dir,
                          "frameCount": converted["provenance"]["frameCount"],
                          "rowCount": converted["provenance"]["rowCount"],
                          "variants": converted["provenance"]["variants"],
                          "outputSha256": converted["provenance"]["outputSha256"]}, sort_keys=True))
        return 0
    except (ReplayConversionError, OSError, TypeError) as exc:
        print(f"dbq_replay_to_evaluator: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())


================================================================================
FILE: tools/fetch_docaligner_reference_assets.py
================================================================================

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Explicitly fetch pinned DocAligner reference test assets (never used by Gradle).

The legacy weight files have unresolved file-specific license scope. This tool
only downloads them when the caller explicitly passes --fetch; it does not
accept license terms, and the assets are ignored by git.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import hashlib
import re
import sys
import urllib.parse
import urllib.request
from http.cookiejar import CookieJar
from pathlib import Path


ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]

UPSTREAM_REVISION = "3275b0f07f8e99d8c01cb0774dea2549be1416b6"
ASSETS = {
    "models/lc100.onnx": (
        "1IlbLPkCv-TdaBLOPh_4J97P1_KHYYJ7a",
        "f4117b786e3a18470f3865c93f3c2bd69d9b998edd60f385574a5c665e79594e",

PNG_SHA256 = "d6966b60720a13a99b190dafcb8922e82133cb52f279b8f7844b391c208a7a99"


def sha256(data: bytes) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()


def read_google_drive(file_id: str) -> bytes:
    """Fetch a public Drive file, following the large-file confirmation token."""
    jar = CookieJar()
    opener = urllib.request.build_opener(urllib.request.HTTPCookieProcessor(jar))
    base = "https://drive.google.com/uc"
    params = {"export": "download", "id": file_id}

    def get(query: dict[str, str]) -> tuple[bytes, str]:
        url = base + "?" + urllib.parse.urlencode(query)
        request = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": "DocScan-reference-assets/1"})
        with opener.open(request, timeout=120) as response:
            return response.read(), response.headers.get("Content-Type", "")

    data, content_type = get(params)
    if "text/html" not in content_type.lower():
        return data

    token = next((cookie.value for cookie in jar if cookie.name.startswith("download_warning")), None)
    if token is None:
        html = data.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
        match = re.search(r"[?&]confirm=([0-9A-Za-z_-]+)", html)
        if match:
            token = match.group(1)
    if token:
        params["confirm"] = token
        data, content_type = get(params)
        if "text/html" not in content_type.lower():
            return data
    raise RuntimeError(
        f"Google Drive returned an HTML confirmation/error page for {file_id}; "
        "check network access or fetch that public file manually."
    )


def write_verified(path: Path, data: bytes, expected_sha: str) -> None:
    actual = sha256(data)
    if actual != expected_sha:
        raise RuntimeError(f"SHA-256 mismatch for {path.name}: expected {expected_sha}, got {actual}")
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    if path.exists():
        existing = path.read_bytes()
        if sha256(existing) != expected_sha:
            raise RuntimeError(f"Refusing to overwrite different local file: {path}")
        return
    path.write_bytes(data)


def fetch(assets_dir: Path) -> None:
    for relative, (source, expected_sha) in ASSETS.items():
        if relative.startswith("models/"):
            payload = read_google_drive(source)
            source_description = f"Google Drive ID {source}"
        else:
            request = urllib.request.Request(source, headers={"User-Agent": "DocScan-reference-assets/1"})
            with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=60) as response:
                payload = response.read()
            source_description = source
        path = assets_dir / relative
        write_verified(path, payload, expected_sha)
        print(f"verified {relative} sha256={expected_sha} ({source_description})")


def make_fixtures(assets_dir: Path) -> None:
    try:
        import cv2
        import numpy as np
    except ImportError as exc:
        raise RuntimeError("Fixture generation requires NumPy and OpenCV; use the pinned reference venv") from exc

    card_jpg = assets_dir / "docaligner_run_test_card.jpg"
    card = cv2.imread(str(card_jpg), cv2.IMREAD_COLOR)
    if card is None:
        raise RuntimeError(f"Missing or unreadable pinned test card: {card_jpg}; run with --fetch")
    card_png = assets_dir / "docaligner_run_test_card.png"
    cv2.imwrite(str(card_png), card)
    actual_png_sha = hashlib.sha256(card_png.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
    if actual_png_sha != PNG_SHA256:
        card_png.unlink(missing_ok=True)
        raise RuntimeError(
            "PNG encoding does not match the recorded test asset hash; use OpenCV 5.0.0.93 "
            f"(expected {PNG_SHA256}, got {actual_png_sha})"
        )

    h, w = 480, 640
    fixtures: dict[str, object] = {
        "negative_white": np.full((h, w, 3), 255, np.uint8),
        "negative_black": np.zeros((h, w, 3), np.uint8),
        "negative_uniform_gray": np.full((h, w, 3), 127, np.uint8),
    }
    rng = np.random.default_rng(20261020)
    fixtures["negative_low_contrast_noise"] = np.clip(
        127 + rng.normal(0, 3, (h, w, 3)), 0, 255
    ).astype(np.uint8)

    scene = np.full((h, w, 3), 92, np.uint8)
    paper = np.array([[92, 54], [550, 78], [525, 424], [111, 406]], np.int32)
    cv2.fillConvexPoly(scene, paper, (224, 224, 224))
    cv2.polylines(scene, [paper], True, (35, 35, 35), 4)
    for y in range(120, 370, 22):
        cv2.line(scene, (155, y), (472 - ((y // 22) % 3) * 24, y), (65, 65, 65), 2)
    fixtures["synthetic_document"] = scene

    panel = np.full((h, w, 3), (135, 94, 52), np.uint8)
    panel_poly = np.array([[125, 43], [528, 91], [495, 420], [102, 383]], np.int32)
    cv2.fillConvexPoly(panel, panel_poly, (29, 150, 222))
    cv2.polylines(panel, [panel_poly], True, (250, 245, 225), 8)
    cv2.putText(panel, "GRAPHIC", (188, 210), cv2.FONT_HERSHEY_SIMPLEX,
                1.4, (245, 245, 245), 4, cv2.LINE_AA)
    cv2.rectangle(panel, (180, 250), (435, 298), (44, 60, 220), -1)
    fixtures["negative_graphic_panel"] = panel

    clutter = np.zeros((h, w, 3), np.uint8)
    for y in range(0, h, 24):
        for x in range(0, w, 24):
            if (x // 24 + y // 24) % 2:
                clutter[y:y + 24, x:x + 24] = (220, 220, 220)
    for i in range(10):
        cv2.circle(clutter, (35 + i * 60, 240 + (i % 3) * 25), 18,
                   (30 + (i * 19) % 210,) * 3, -1)
    fixtures["negative_checker_clutter"] = clutter

    for name, image in fixtures.items():
        path = assets_dir / f"{name}.png"
        if not cv2.imwrite(str(path), image):
            raise RuntimeError(f"Unable to write fixture: {path}")
    print(f"generated {len(fixtures) + 1} PNG fixtures; test card sha256={actual_png_sha}")


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--assets-dir", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_ASSETS)
    parser.add_argument("--fetch", action="store_true", help="explicitly download the two pinned legacy models and pinned upstream JPEG")
    parser.add_argument("--generate-fixtures", action="store_true", help="generate ignored PNG fixtures using local OpenCV/NumPy")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    if not args.fetch and not args.generate_fixtures:
        parser.error("nothing requested; pass --fetch and/or --generate-fixtures explicitly")
    if args.fetch:
        fetch(args.assets_dir)
    if args.generate_fixtures:
        make_fixtures(args.assets_dir)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    try:
        raise SystemExit(main())
    except Exception as error:
        print(f"error: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
        raise SystemExit(1)


================================================================================
FILE: tools/ml/edge_snap.py
================================================================================

"""Prototype of the still-image edge snapper (mirrored in Kotlin as SheetEdgeSnapper).

For every side of a coarse quad: sample brightness profiles along the outward normal (strip-averaged, smoothed),
pick for each position the strongest transition of the side's polarity near the coarse edge, fit a line robustly
(IRLS with Tukey weights), then intersect neighbouring lines. A side that cannot be confirmed keeps its coarse line.
"""
import cv2
import numpy as np


def _profiles(gray, a, b, normal, R, n=48, strip=2):
    """Returns (ts, offsets, P[n, 2R+1]) brightness profiles along `normal` (outward) from points on a->b."""
    ts = np.linspace(0.08, 0.92, n)
    d = b - a
    tang = d / (np.linalg.norm(d) + 1e-9)
    offs = np.arange(-R, R + 1, dtype=np.float32)
    P = np.zeros((n, len(offs)), np.float32)
    acc = np.zeros_like(P)
    for k in range(-strip, strip + 1):
        pts = (a[None, :] + ts[:, None] * d[None, :] + k * 2.0 * tang[None, :])  # n x 2
        xs = pts[:, 0:1] + normal[0] * offs[None, :]
        ys = pts[:, 1:2] + normal[1] * offs[None, :]
        acc += cv2.remap(gray, xs.astype(np.float32), ys.astype(np.float32), cv2.INTER_LINEAR, borderMode=cv2.BORDER_REPLICATE)
    P = acc / (2 * strip + 1)
    P = cv2.GaussianBlur(P, (1, 0), sigmaX=0, sigmaY=0) if False else cv2.GaussianBlur(P, (0, 0), sigmaX=1.6, sigmaY=0.01)
    return ts, offs, P


def snap(gray, quad, R=26, min_support=0.35):
    q = np.asarray(quad, np.float32)
    c = q.mean(0)
    lines = []
    info = []
    for i in range(4):
        a, b = q[i], q[(i + 1) % 4]
        d = (b - a) / (np.linalg.norm(b - a) + 1e-9)
        n = np.array([d[1], -d[0]], np.float32)
        if np.dot(n, (a + b) / 2 - c) < 0:
            n = -n                                  # outward
        ts, offs, P = _profiles(gray, a, b, n, R)
        mid = len(offs) // 2
        inner = P[:, mid - 12:mid - 4].mean(1)
        outer = P[:, mid + 4:mid + 12].mean(1)
        polarity = 1.0 if np.median(inner - outer) >= 0 else -1.0    # +1: paper brighter than background
        G = np.zeros_like(P)
        G[:, 1:-1] = (P[:, :-2] - P[:, 2:]) * polarity / 2.0         # large where inside is brighter than outside (paper polarity)
        # prefer transitions near the coarse edge
        weight = 1.0 - 0.45 * np.abs(offs) / R
        score = G * weight[None, :]
        best = score.argmax(1)
        strength = G[np.arange(len(ts)), best]
        ok = strength > 6.0
        s = offs[best]
        pts_t, pts_s = ts[ok], s[ok]
        if len(pts_t) < min_support * len(ts):
            lines.append((a, d, None)); info.append(("weak", len(pts_t))); continue
        # IRLS line s(t) = s0 + s1*t with Tukey weights
        w = np.ones_like(pts_t)
        for _ in range(8):
            A = np.stack([np.ones_like(pts_t), pts_t], 1) * w[:, None]
            coef, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(A, pts_s * w, rcond=None)
            res = pts_s - (coef[0] + coef[1] * pts_t)
            sigma = max(1.0, 1.4826 * np.median(np.abs(res)))
            u = res / (4.685 * sigma)
            w = np.where(np.abs(u) < 1, (1 - u ** 2) ** 2, 0.0)
        inl = np.abs(pts_s - (coef[0] + coef[1] * pts_t)) < 3.0
        if inl.sum() < min_support * len(ts) or len(np.unique((pts_t[inl] * 8).astype(int))) < 5:
            lines.append((a, d, None)); info.append(("few-inliers", int(inl.sum()))); continue
        # refit on inliers
        A = np.stack([np.ones(inl.sum()), pts_t[inl]], 1)
        coef, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(A, pts_s[inl], rcond=None)
        pa = a + n * coef[0]
        pb = b + n * (coef[0] + coef[1])
        dd = (pb - pa) / (np.linalg.norm(pb - pa) + 1e-9)
        lines.append((pa, dd, True)); info.append(("ok", int(inl.sum())))
    new = []
    for i in range(4):
        p1, d1, _ = lines[(i + 3) % 4]
        p2, d2, _ = lines[i]
        M = np.array([d1, -d2], np.float32).T
        if abs(np.linalg.det(M)) < 1e-4:
            new.append(q[i]); continue
        t = np.linalg.solve(M, p2 - p1)
        pt = p1 + t[0] * d1
        # a corner may not move farther than the search window allows (diagonal)
        if np.linalg.norm(pt - q[i]) > R * 1.8:
            pt = q[i]
        new.append(pt)
    return np.array(new, np.float32), info


if __name__ == "__main__":
    import sys
    sys.path.insert(0, ".")
    import torch, train, quad as Q
    img_path, weights, out = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]
    img = cv2.imread(img_path)
    H, W = img.shape[:2]
    scale = 1600 / max(H, W)
    work = cv2.resize(img, (int(W * scale), int(H * scale)), interpolation=cv2.INTER_AREA) if scale < 1 else img
    h, w = work.shape[:2]
    m = train.Wrapped(train.build_model(False)); m.load_state_dict(torch.load(weights, map_location="cpu")); m.eval()
    s = cv2.resize(work, (256, 256), interpolation=cv2.INTER_AREA)
    with torch.no_grad():
        prob = torch.sigmoid(m(torch.from_numpy(s[..., ::-1].copy()).permute(2, 0, 1).float()[None] / 255))[0, 0].numpy()
    q, conf = Q.mask_to_quad(prob)
    coarse = q * np.array([w / 256, h / 256], np.float32)
    gray = cv2.cvtColor(work, cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY)
    refined, info = snap(gray, coarse)
    print("conf", round(conf, 3), info)
    print("coarse ", np.round(coarse / [w, h], 4).tolist())
    print("refined", np.round(refined / [w, h], 4).tolist())
    vis = work.copy()
    cv2.polylines(vis, [coarse.astype(np.int32)], True, (0, 0, 255), 2)
    cv2.polylines(vis, [refined.astype(np.int32)], True, (0, 255, 0), 2)
    cv2.imwrite(out, vis)


================================================================================
FILE: tools/ml/eval.py
================================================================================

"""Evaluate a trained model on fresh synthetic samples (and a folder of labeled real photos if given).

  python tools/ml/eval.py ~/DocScanML/run1/model.pt [--n 400]
Reports detection rate, false-positive rate on no-document samples, mask IoU, corner error (% of diagonal)
for documents fully inside the frame.
"""
import argparse
import sys

import numpy as np
import torch

import quad as Q
import synth
import train


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("weights")
    ap.add_argument("--n", type=int, default=400)
    a = ap.parse_args()
    model = train.Wrapped(train.build_model(pretrained=False))
    model.load_state_dict(torch.load(a.weights, map_location="cpu"))
    model.eval()
    rng = np.random.default_rng(12345)
    import random
    random.seed(5)
    S = train.SIZE
    diag = (S * S * 2) ** 0.5
    tp = fn = fp = tn = 0
    ious, errs = [], []
    for _ in range(a.n):
        img, mask, q = synth.sample(rng, (S, S))
        x = torch.from_numpy(img).permute(2, 0, 1).float()[None] / 255.0
        with torch.no_grad():
            prob = torch.sigmoid(model(x))[0, 0].numpy()
        pq, conf = Q.mask_to_quad(prob)
        if mask.any():
            if pq is None:
                fn += 1
                continue
            tp += 1
            pm = prob > 0.5
            ious.append((pm & (mask > 0)).sum() / max(1, (pm | (mask > 0)).sum()))
            if q is not None and (q >= 2).all() and (q <= S - 3).all():
                errs.append(np.linalg.norm(Q.order(q) - pq, axis=1).mean() / diag * 100)
        else:
            fp += pq is not None
            tn += pq is None
    print(f"docs: detected {tp}/{tp + fn}; no-doc false positives {fp}/{fp + tn}")
    print(f"mask IoU mean {np.mean(ious):.3f} median {np.median(ious):.3f}")
    if errs:
        e = np.array(errs)
        print(f"corner error % diag (fully visible docs, n={len(e)}): mean {e.mean():.2f} median {np.median(e):.2f} p90 {np.percentile(e, 90):.2f}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()


================================================================================
FILE: tools/ml/export_onnx.py
